Act as the audit coordinator for this repository. Build and execute a reproducible,
multi-model smart-contract security audit using the strategy below.

PROJECT: [PROJECT NAME]
REPOSITORY: [PATH OR URL]
TARGET: [COMMIT SHA, OR RESOLVE AND RECORD CURRENT HEAD]
SCOPE: [PRODUCTION SOURCE PATHS; OTHERWISE INVENTORY AND PROPOSE THE SCOPE]
CHAINS / DEPENDENCIES: [IF KNOWN]

Adapt the strategy to this project's architecture. Do not copy another project's
contract assumptions, compiler settings, source counts, accepted risks, or findings.

This request authorizes local audit preparation, independent model reviews,
static analysis, local fuzzing, symbolic execution, and local exploit-reproduction
tests against isolated copies of this project's source. It does not authorize
production remediation, deployment, live transactions, or purchasing services.

1. ESTABLISH AND FREEZE THE TARGET

Read applicable AGENTS.md files and inspect repository state before acting.
Preserve unrelated changes. Identify the exact code being audited, including
uncommitted production changes if present; never silently omit them.

Create an immutable audit snapshot and record:
- Full commit SHA and working-tree differences.
- Production source, interfaces, reachable dependencies, and explicit exclusions.
- Source hashes and dependency/submodule revisions.
- Compiler versions, optimizer settings, EVM target, via-IR, metadata settings,
  remappings, lockfiles, and relevant build/deployment configuration.
- Each separately compiled package or compiler profile.

Keep production source and frozen build inputs unchanged throughout this round.
Put audit tests, reports, logs, caches, and harness runtimes in isolated locations.
Verify frozen bytes before and after each attempt.

Do not weaken existing freeze enforcement. A finding does not authorize a fix.
Remediation requires a separate decision, a new candidate, and targeted re-audit.

2. CREATE THE AUDIT CONTROL PACKAGE

Create audits/<round>/ containing:
- PLAN.md
- SCOPE.md and scope-files.txt
- freeze.json and a freeze verification procedure
- STATUS.md
- matrix.json with every required run
- toolchain.json with exact versions and configurations
- clean reviewer prompts
- runs/<slot>/<attempt>/
- reconciliation/
- FINAL-AUDIT-REPORT.md

Give every run a stable ID. Track workflow completion, source coverage,
model identity, findings, and limitations separately.

Do not report planned reviews or successful availability probes as completed audits.

3. MODEL MATRIX

Use these requested reviewers:
A. OpenAI GPT-6 Astra, exact available model ID, highest supported reasoning.
B. Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5, exact available model ID, highest supported effort.
C. The strongest accessible Gemini suitable for deep code review, selected from
   current official documentation and actual account access.

For Gemini, investigate available Pro and other suitable reasoning models.
Do not automatically choose Flash because its version number is newer.
Do not invent private model IDs or claim access without evidence.

Run EACH of the five harnesses below separately with EACH of A, B, and C:
five harnesses × three providers = fifteen required harness/model cells.

Also run three independent supplementary reviews:
- GPT-6 Astra: accounting, custody, and economic invariants.
- GPT-6 Astra: authority, lifecycle, and cross-contract composition.
- GPT-6.1 Sol: independent whole-system review.

These supplementary reviews do not replace any harness cell.

If Daybreak Blue is available, record it as a separate optional lane with its
resolved identity and access evidence. Do not infer its underlying model from
an alias or describe ordinary GPT access as Daybreak access.

Model selection must happen in the actual runner. A prompt cannot select a model.
Record requested model, accepted local selection, provider-returned identity,
reasoning/thinking settings, runner version, and every fallback separately.
Missing provider-returned fields remain unknown.

Disable automatic fallback. An unavailable requested route is BLOCKED.
Do not silently substitute a cheaper model or role-play another provider.

4. THE FIVE HARNESSES

Use the actual upstream workflows:

- 0xSimao AI:
  https://github.com/0xsimao/0xsimao-ai

- Pashov Skills / solidity-auditor:
  https://github.com/pashov/skills

- OpenKritt:
  https://github.com/Kritt-ai/open-kritt

- Trail of Bits Skills:
  https://github.com/trailofbits/skills

- Gebal:
  https://github.com/Heesho/gebal

Resolve and pin an appropriate reviewed revision of each before execution.
Record upstream URL, commit, local modifications, loaded resources, and hashes.
Install runtimes outside the frozen source tree.

Historical reference revisions from our previous setup:
- 0xSimao: 3f81e5803174182a7db07eca87849d2b3d571113
- Pashov: 8ce544c9c9affab448d3dc4c79191d052e3a57ec
- OpenKritt: 43e1d19a00ce50bd93253d1c6c3a48cfffbcc4c3
- Trail of Bits: 82fe8226252622fa807643bdca1710901198553a
- Gebal: 5c68ec0284dc642823abe81cbc0e02fcb080a69f

These are historical pins, not claims about latest releases. Inspect compatibility
and provenance before choosing a pin. Any modified controller is a distinct method.

Harness-specific requirements:
- 0xSimao: execute every required perspective, adjudication, and proof stage;
  retain evidence before automatic cleanup. Explicitly include interfaces.
- Pashov: execute required specialists and judge; record each stage's actual
  model/effort. Disable prior-project memory and repeated-run finding memory.
- OpenKritt: pin the engine AND exact workflow, injected skills, ranker,
  post-processing, stage counts, and configurations. Use a clean runtime.
- Trail of Bits: declare the exact skill aggregate. At minimum include
  entry-point-analyzer, token-integration-analyzer, and guidelines-advisor.
  Add applicable context-building, spec-to-code, and secure-workflow skills as
  separately declared stages. Do not call a three-skill aggregate the full catalog.
- Gebal: preserve native snapshot/context hashes and origin-bound imports.
  Keep cold model review and test-inclusive deterministic runs separately bound.
  Add a disclosed test-exposed review afterward where useful. Never change hashes
  to import a review into a different source context.

Run full declared methods where supported. A generic prompt inspired by a harness
is not execution of that harness. Missing specialists, proof stages, or unsupported
provider routing leave the cell BLOCKED or INCOMPLETE.

5. PRESERVE INDEPENDENCE

Use a fresh context and isolated output directory for every cell and specialist.
Parallel agent execution is authorized where isolation and resources permit it.

Before first-pass sealing, exclude:
- Previous audit findings and reports.
- Other reviewers' conclusions.
- Accepted-risk lists that reveal historical findings.
- Historical harness memory or databases.
- Separate scanner-campaign results.
- Finding-revealing historical tests.

Provide the same frozen source, reachable dependency context, and clean design
specification to every reviewer. Document unavoidable exposure.

Harness-native tools remain part of that harness's declared method. Disclose their
ordering and distinguish tool-assisted review from a source-only first pass.

Seal FIRST-PASS.md with timestamp and SHA-256 before cross-run reconciliation.
Preserve original reports; append corrections rather than rewriting history.

6. TOOL CAMPAIGNS

Run and retain evidence for all four core campaigns:
- Slither: applicable detectors and architecture/entry-point/call-graph printers.
- Aderyn: independent static analysis with individual alert triage.
- Echidna: project-specific stateful property campaigns.
- Halmos: targeted symbolic checks for critical accounting and authorization.

Also run the project's applicable validation stack:
- Foundry build and regression tests.
- Foundry fuzz tests and stateful invariants.
- Coverage and gas/size checks, with instrumentation limitations disclosed.
- Anvil/local forks for dependency and integration behavior when relevant.
- Hardhat compilation/tests if maintained by the project.
- Solidity linting and formatting checks without rewriting frozen source.
- ABI, SDK, frontend, indexer, artifact, and deployment-script checks where relevant.
- Source/compiler/artifact and deployed-bytecode comparison if deployed code is
  explicitly in scope.

Evaluate these additional tools and give each an applicability disposition:
- Medusa for a second stateful fuzzing engine.
- Mutation testing to assess whether important properties detect broken behavior.
- Certora for selected high-value formal specifications, if available and authorized.
- SMTChecker or another supported verifier for suitable isolated properties.
- Dependency and supply-chain checks for the actual package ecosystem.

Do not buy tools or services automatically. Optional unavailable tools remain
explicitly unavailable; do not pretend another tool supplied their evidence.

Derive commands from the actual repository and installed tool versions.
Pin configurations, record reproducible seeds, and execute all compiler profiles.
Avoid concurrent jobs sharing mutable build outputs.

For every campaign retain commands, versions, raw outputs, exit codes, duration,
seeds, run counts, depth, calls, rejected inputs, reverts, coverage, solver bounds,
timeouts, skipped cases, and configuration.

A scanner finding is an observation requiring triage.
No counterexample in a bounded campaign is not a proof.
A timeout, setup revert, crash, or unsupported path is not a pass.
Concrete regression controls do not count as symbolic proofs.

If tool compatibility requires an altered build, preserve the original failure
and label the altered build as a separate compatibility experiment. Do not
change frozen production settings or claim identical bytecode without evidence.

Set explicit campaign and retry budgets. After reasonable targeted diagnostics,
report unresolved proof obligations instead of retrying indefinitely.

7. REVIEW AND PROPERTY DESIGN

Map the complete architecture, authority graph, asset flows, external calls,
entry points, state transitions, and failure/rollback behavior.

Derive independent invariants before writing assertions:
- Asset custody and solvency against liabilities.
- Supply, minting, burning, escrow, shares, and pending accrual.
- Deposits, withdrawals, fees, rewards, rounding, dust, and distribution.
- Authorization, ownership transitions, upgradeability, and initialization.
- Atomic rollback and cross-contract consistency.
- Signature nonces, replay domains, allowances, deadlines, and slippage.
- Oracle freshness/manipulation, flash liquidity, MEV, and ordering where relevant.
- Token callbacks and nonstandard token behavior against declared assumptions.
- Gas-bounded liveness and dependency failure behavior.

Use multiple actors and meaningful sequences. Review the handlers themselves.
Report unreachable actions, excessive assumptions, vacuous assertions, and
properties that merely restate implementation.

Use independently derived reference mathematics with explicit units and rounding.
Test lifecycle boundaries and adversarial local sequences. Keep exploit tests and
fork execution inside isolated local environments.

8. RECONCILIATION

After first-pass seals, compare reviewers, scanner observations, tests, and
historical reports. Deduplicate by root cause while preserving every original ID.

For each finding record:
- Stable ID, severity, and confidence.
- Exact affected source revision and file/line evidence.
- Violated property and practical impact.
- Preconditions and attacker or privileged capabilities.
- Local reproduction or a precise reason reproduction remains incomplete.
- Proposed remedy and regression/property coverage.
- Independent validation or rebuttal.
- Final disposition and remaining uncertainty.

Distinguish confirmed defects, intended behavior, accepted limitations,
configuration risks, integration defects, false positives, and unresolved leads.

Do not use model agreement as proof or count duplicate observations as independent
vulnerabilities. Preserve disagreements and explain the evidence resolving them.
Do not invent owner acceptance.

9. DELIVERY AND COMPLETION

Deliver:
- Executive assessment and prioritized findings.
- Complete fifteen-cell harness/provider matrix and supplementary-review results.
- Per-file and per-property coverage with explicit gaps.
- Tool-campaign results and every incomplete proof obligation.
- Reproduction tests, raw evidence, hashes, and exact rerun instructions.
- Dependency, configuration, deployment, and integration limitations.
- Proposed remediation order and targeted re-audit plan.
- Final source-integrity verification.

Track COMPLETE, INCOMPLETE, BLOCKED, NOT_RUN, and NOT_APPLICABLE accurately.
Keep workflow completion distinct from security findings and release readiness.
A finished queue does not establish completed coverage or security approval.

Begin with repository discovery, immutable target capture, and preparation of
the executable audit matrix. Continue with authorized local work. If one lane
is blocked, document it and continue independent eligible lanes.

Do not remediate production contracts, publish findings, deploy, broadcast
transactions, or claim external-auditor certification as part of this task.

## Assessment

The review identifies two principal source-level root causes. The more consequential is conditional on the prize contract: a dishonest or later nontransferable NFT can leave a winner without the promised prize even though the sponsor can receive 95% of sales. Reviewers disagree on whether this is a High design violation, a Medium integration flaw or an explicitly limited prize-trust guarantee. The disagreement arises from conflicting scope language and remains open.

The second is a Low destination-safety failure. A sponsor can choose the address of a future raffle as its fixed recipient. After that raffle exists, the first raffle can send an ordinary ERC721 prize into it, where the prize becomes unrecoverable. A local honest-token reproduction passed. The demonstrated loss belongs to the sponsor-selected recipient; it does not show theft from an arbitrary EOA or another raffle's accounted funds.

Completed testing provides substantial evidence for ordinary custody, allocation, authorization and lifecycle behavior. It does not remove the prize-trust issue, prove all external integrations, or make weakly exercised invariant handlers comprehensive. There is no demonstrated unconditional Critical exploit or production quote-ledger insolvency in the reconciled evidence.

The register contains 21 findings, observations, configuration risks, closed candidates and advisory entries—not 21 vulnerabilities. Its 190 attribution records plus the two late Pashov attributions preserve every adopted original ID, including rejected candidates and conflicting severity judgments. Eighteen sealed first-pass report paths underpin the combined reconciliation; repeated paths, report copies, functions and model agreement are not independent votes. OpenKritt's four native candidate records are separately identified and deduplicated. ## Findings

### RF-001 — Prize delivery is conditional while NFT-outcome proceeds are independently payable

**Severity:** High under the explicit untrusted-prize DESIGN requirement; Medium or Low/integration risk under other reviewers' interpretation of the honest, standards-compliant prize assumption. **Confidence:** high in the reachable behavior; unresolved classification because the scope statements conflict.

A sponsor chooses a prize contract that either fabricates escrow/delivery statements or genuinely escrows an NFT and later refuses, pauses or revokes transferability. The factory checks that token's callback, Active status and ownerOf response. Buyers then purchase entries and the normal VRF path resolves NftWon. Settlement makes sponsor proceeds and protocol fees available without first delivering the prize. A prior successful payout is not rolled back by a later failed redemption, and NftWon has no failed-delivery refund transition.

The sponsor needs control over the selected collection's dishonest implementation or relevant transfer authority, or an external collection failure must occur. Quote-token or VRF compromise is not required. The economic exposure is 95% of sales paid to the sponsor while the winner lacks an enforceable promised NFT. The quote ledger can remain exactly solvent throughout. This is not demonstrated against a truthful NFT that stays transferable, and no other clone is drained.

Source anchors: [factory admission and escrow](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/clean-context/packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol:127), [prize receipt](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/clean-context/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:416), [redemption and verification](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/clean-context/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:309), [independent proceeds release](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/clean-context/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:375) and [terminal allocation](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/clean-context/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:533). The scope conflict is recorded between DESIGN.md and IRaffle.sol:12–15. Earlier sealed fabrication mocks support a concrete artificial-token path; their separate ownership ledger illustrates dishonest semantics rather than proving the value or behavior of a deployed collection. Incoming claimed proofs are not automatically independent validation.

Daybreak Simao H-1 through H-5 cover different functions of this economic chain. Late Pashov findings 1 and 2 have confidence 90, not an assigned security severity. Claude TIA-1/TOB-S6-3 and Gemini FP-M-02 use Medium; Claude SUP-03 calls it a Low integration risk and explicitly not a code defect. Those judgments remain visible. No reviewer statement is treated as owner risk acceptance.

Before implementation, specify whether the product promises enforceable prize delivery or only interaction with approved/trusted collection semantics. An allowlist can restrict exposure but cannot itself prevent later upgrades, pauses or seizure. A funded failure fallback must retain all quote amounts it promises, including protocol fees, and handle settlement and payout order explicitly. Simply checking ownerOf again does not authenticate a malicious token. No patch was applied.

### RF-002 — A future clone recipient bypasses creation-time destination screening

**Severity:** Low. **Confidence:** high for the demonstrated sponsor-return path.

A sponsor configures raffle A's immutable recipient as the predictable address of future raffle B. That address has no code and is not yet registered, so creation checks accept it. B is then normally deployed. If A refunds or takes the cash branch, anyone can call releaseSponsorPrize; its plain transferFrom sends A's NFT to B without repeating the runtime protocol-destination screen used by quote payouts. B exposes exits only for its own configured prize, leaving A's prize stuck.

The root reproduction used an honest ERC721 and both real clones. It confirms cross-clone asset movement and sponsor-selected own loss. Quote payout screening can instead leave A's sponsor proceeds unclaimable. The proof does not show an attacker choosing an unrelated victim's recipient. It also does not show B redeeming an A ticket: redemption requires the current owner to originate the call, which B cannot do.

Source anchors: [CREATE clone and registration](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/clean-context/packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol:105), [recipient validation](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/clean-context/packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol:163), [sponsor prize release](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/clean-context/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:395) and [runtime quote screen](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/clean-context/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:564). Reproduction: [RecipientValidation.t.sol](/Users/hishamel-husseini/Documents/projects/raffle-fun/audits/2026-10-21-r001/reconciliation/recipient-validation/RecipientValidation.t.sol) and [passing log](/Users/hishamel-husseini/Documents/projects/raffle-fun/audits/2026-10-21-r001/runs/TOOL-RECIPIENT-VALIDATION/attempt-01/stdout.txt).

Simao J-4 rejects the candidate as self-harm; Gemini's grouped FP-M-01 assigns Medium; Claude SUP-01 assigns Low. The register retains the Low destination-invariant defect and its strict preconditions. Apply a consistent runtime NFT destination policy if this invariant is required. Refusing the transfer prevents cross-clone movement but does not recover an immutable stranded claim; any recovery mechanism requires a separate authority and design decision. Changing CREATE to CREATE2 or adding address randomness is not a complete recovery or destination-safety solution.

## Test assurance and remediation-proposal quality

The four-mutant campaign tested fee allocation, an owner guard, a deadline comparison and disabled purchases in disposable copies. All four compiled and were killed by existing unit/fuzz/security tests. All four initially survived short invariant runs. The fee mutant was eventually killed at the larger recorded run count, while completely disabled purchases still passed strict invariants because failures were caught inside the handler. This constrains the meaning of large successful call counters. See [mutation report](/Users/hishamel-husseini/Documents/projects/raffle-fun/audits/2026-10-21-r001/runs/TOOL-MUTATION-QUALITY/SUMMARY.md).

| ID | Assurance issue |
|---|---|
| AQ-001 | Swallowed reverts/no-op paths can leave every economic action inactive while invariants pass. |
| AQ-002 | Handlers select the actual ticket owner, so they do not exercise the adversarial caller needed to expose owner-check deletion. |
| AQ-003 | Deadline prefilters omit the forbidden exact boundary and can conceal rejection-boundary mutations. |
| AQ-004 | Independent allocation checks are useful, but short-run branch reachability is weak and some ghost values follow implementation state. |
| AQ-005 | The standalone Python model does not roll back lazy settlement on rejected unauthorized redemption. Solidity does roll back; passing Python tests are not an equivalence proof. |
| AQ-006 | Eleven of 52 historical mutation definitions do not match the current target. Invalid definitions are not surviving mutants and must not inflate the score. |
| AQ-007 | Partial or rejected workflows, missing source-context files and uncertain model identity must not be reported as completed assurance. Excluded tests do not establish repository-wide test absence. |
| AQ-008 | The late Pashov Option C patch is unvalidated and incorrectly migrates zero terminal balances when NftWon is still unsettled, leaving the pot outside its proposed refund liability. This is a flaw in a suggestion, not frozen production code. |

The proposed Option C is excluded from recommended implementation. Any delivery fallback must cover pre-settlement and settled NftWon, move each liability exactly once, retain all promised money and define successful delivery and previously paid claims. No proposal has been applied or accepted by the owner.

## Campaign interpretation

The release run reports 79 passes, no failures and one unconfigured RPC-fork skip; nine fuzz tests ran 100,000 cases each. The nine invariant results report **233,698,304 calls** in total. These are native counters, not independent successful economic actions: handlers catch reverts and can return without acting. The [actual counter ledger](runs/TOOL-RELEASE-EXTENDED/attempt-01/campaign-statistics-final.json) preserves per-property runs/calls. Both extended Echidna campaigns reached their actual limits (100,040 and 100,077 calls), six properties passing each, one worker, sequence length100 and seeds2026102101/02. Their [assessments](ECHIDNA-EXTENDED-RESULTS.json) preserve native instruction/corpus counters. Medusa passed26native checks including6actual properties; the other20 are not additional independent invariants.

Halmos originals cover two independently symbolic purchase amounts1..16, two owners/tickets, exact-transfer quote and fixed VRF mocks. Refund covers both refund orders (512tuples), cash all winning positions and two sponsor-release orders (8704tuples), NFT all winning positions with fixed payout order (4352tuples). Loop bound3 did not truncate completed execution (zero bounded/blocked paths). Three accounting properties passed directly; stronger successful-completion path exploration had timeouts whose11exact residual queries were all discharged UNSAT after unchanged Halmos arithmetic refinement and alternate solvers. Native timeouts remain recorded. [Sealed summary and exact closure](runs/TOOL-HALMOS-CONTINUATION/SUMMARY.md) give all domains, solvers and scripts. This is no universal proof over arbitrary actors, amounts, transfers, callbacks, malicious tokens or payout permutations.

The [mutation campaign](runs/TOOL-MUTATION-QUALITY/SUMMARY.md) demonstrates assertion quality and gaps: all4valid mutants were killed by the existing unit/fuzz/security selection, all4survived short invariants, the fee mutant was later killed at120invariant runs, and completely disabled purchases still pass strict invariants. Eleven of52historical mutation definitions do not match this target; they are invalid definitions, not surviving mutants. The Python model’s rejected lazy redemption lacks EVM rollback; its11passing standalone tests do not prove model equivalence.

No live candidate instance was supplied. Both maintained mainnet/Sepolia fork tests subsequently passed at explicit block/hash pins; [fork evidence](PUBLIC-FORK-VALIDATION.md) verifies the actual quote purchase and local wrapper request paths with mock prize and cheatcode funding. Live candidate-bytecode identity, complete external-administration review, chain finality and genuine offchain fulfillment remain unproved. Certora supplied no evidence. Halmos is the supported executed verifier; standalone SMTChecker supplied no successful verdict. Any external lane’s incomplete native stages, wrong/missing dependency context or unverified model selection remain visible separately in [matrix.json](matrix.json) and [provider validation](PROVIDER-HANDOFF-VALIDATION.md).

| Custom signed messages, EIP-712 domains, permit nonces | NOT_APPLICABLE to the five production files: no custom signature/permit verification surface. Ordinary transaction nonces and external quote-token approvals are not implemented by the raffle contracts. ERC721 owner/operator authorization is reviewed and tested separately. |
| Upgrade/admin transitions | No mutable upgrade or protocol administrator entry point in this candidate. Constructor configuration, implementation lock, clone initialization and fixed beneficiary authority are in scope. A new recovery or upgrade role would require a new authority review. |
| AMM slippage, lending liquidation, leverage and flash liquidity | NOT_APPLICABLE as protocol mechanisms: this is a fixed-price entry sale, with an openly configured reserve branch. Secondary-market ordering remains a conditional integration lead rather than a proved primary-sale exploit. |
| Cross-chain messages/bridges | NOT_APPLICABLE: no bridge or cross-chain message verification in these production files. Chain-specific deployment/finality remains an external configuration gap. |
| Price-oracle freshness | No direct price-feed read is implemented. The trusted wrapper supplies a native fee quote; its internal pricing/fallback behavior and live configuration are outside the reviewed interface closure. VRF authentication, request binding, fee quotation and hard callback/request deadlines are applicable and separately reviewed. |
| Shares, interest and recurring rewards | NOT_APPLICABLE: no vault-share, lending-interest or reward-accrual ledger. The relevant units are quote-token micro-units, entry counts, bearer range tickets and pending terminal liabilities. |

These dispositions are source-scope statements, not assertions that excluded frontend, wallet, token or chain code lacks those mechanisms.

The incremental check verified80hash records and all referenced line bounds without mismatch; this is not whole-package integrity verification.

## Late source evidence

The native Gemini OpenKritt engine completed112logical jobs:1mapping,23flows and88investigations. It produced zero finding records. Three transport failures and the disclosed native queue resume remain in the evidence. With zero candidates, native ranker/deduplication/postprocessing model calls had no eligible work and were not executed. The actual native engine, official CLI High route,43frozen inputs and lifecycle records are sealed. Its owned engine, bridge, exporter and keep-awake processes are stopped. Zero output does not refute other findings or prove safety.

The sealed Gemini Trail of Bits attempt04 adds a real logged paused-prize mock execution supporting RF-001. Its recipient test uses impersonation of a contract unable to initiate redemption, so it does not prove practical winner-custody loss. The root's separate honest-ERC721 future-clone test supports the narrower sponsor-selected recipient sequence. Source assertions, missing-test claims from deliberately excluded context and the S5 denominator error are corrected separately. S5 checked10of219raw requirements, leaving209unchecked; six-stage transport/workflow qualifications remain explicit.

The Gemini Simao attempt04 judge completed native SUCCESS. Its43source hashes,12original leaf report/receipt pairs and artifact seal verified. Its12final entries,40raw IDs and12unnumbered lead summaries are preserved. Independent final method-semantic qualification remains unchecked. Gemini Pashov attempt04 retains strict native ERROR after a stream interruption; later DONE output and assembler exit0 support artifact preservation, not method completion. Its9confidence-scored entries,8leads,17canonical groups and33raw IDs are retained as sealed hypotheses. Confidence90/85/75 is not severity. Neither artifact adoption completes the unavailable root semantic gate.

## Findings and disagreements

RF-001 is the conditional prize-admission/delivery/proceeds chain. A dishonest or later nontransferable prize can defeat promised economic delivery while independently payable proceeds have already left. Quote liabilities can still balance exactly. The register preserves conditional High, Medium, Low/integration and scope disagreements. Honest continuously transferable ERC721 semantics and arbitrary adversarial prizes are different guarantees; no owner acceptance or scope relaxation is inferred. Incoming named collection examples are not independently verified live-deployment proofs.

RF-002 is a narrow sponsor-selected future-clone recipient hazard. The sponsor configures an undeployed clone address, the clone later exists, and unsafe prize return can strand the sponsor's own NFT there. This has an executed honest-token reproduction. It is not unrestricted theft from EOAs. A future clone can own a ticket yet lack the ability to originate redemption. Treasury collisions differ: matching-clone initialization fails before registry insertion, so the practical risk is creation-nonce liveness.

New Simao/Pashov economic findings remain disputed. Sponsor paid purchases, odds dilution before the deadline, reserve crossing, cash-outcome shares and the loss of the empty-cancellation exception after a paid entry follow disclosed rules. The register preserves native ratings/confidence and CLOSED-002/CLOSED-004 dispositions rather than promoting disagreement into proof. Extreme public reserve, recipient capability, issuer freeze, VRF fee/service availability and callback event ordering retain their distinct configuration/integration classifications.

## Remediation and re-audit order

First resolve the supported prize trust model. A delivery-linked payout/refund design must cover both sponsor and treasury claims, pre-settlement and settled liabilities, already delivered prizes, paid claims, deliberate winner inaction and dishonest getters. A payment guard alone cannot authenticate a malicious token. No earlier OptionC or incoming sample diff is a ready patch.

Next define recipient authority and failed-delivery behavior. Re-audit actual callable contract holders, sponsor-selected future clones, distinct quote/NFT destinations and rollback across terminal exits. Do not redirect a configured prize recipient automatically without an approved beneficiary policy.

Then verify intended deployment identities, immutable inputs, supported token behavior and wrapper service operation. Pinned public-fork tests passed the actual USDC/wrapper request paths, but genuine offchain fulfillment, live candidate binding and ongoing issuer/provider guarantees remain unverified.

Finally strengthen assurance: reachable multi-actor handlers, non-vacuous successful-action counts, independent reference math, rollback-faithful Python modeling, realistic contract caller paths and mutation effectiveness. Preserve all bounded domains and earlier timeouts/skips. Any authorized source revision needs fresh relevant tests and symbolic obligations; none was applied here.

## Remaining receipts and ownership

Four source receipts remain pending: DAYBREAK-TOB attempt03, CLAUDE-TOB S6 attempt02, native CLAUDE-OPENKRITT, and the CLAUDE-SIMAO public-evidence variant. Metadata at22:37UTC shows Daybreak ToB still running; Claude S6 and public-evidence Simao have terminal results but no eligible sealed source receipt was adopted. No Anthropic/Gemini rejection is inferred from the OpenAI coordinator rejection.

The existing receipt watcher PID68662 continues to observe sealed receipts only. It does not read unsealed findings, approve methods or start model continuations. Its lifecycle must be recorded before any future global package seal. Final source reconciliation and global audit completion are not claimed. No source edits, deployments, live transactions or owner acceptance occurred.

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for AI/code agents (and humans skimming for the essentials) working in the
open·kritt repo. This is the canonical agent guide; `CLAUDE.md` points here.

Read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the full contributor flow — this file is
the fast, do/don't version.

## What this is

open·kritt is an AI-driven security vulnerability scanner. It's a **polyglot
monorepo** of cooperating services:

| Path             | What                                          | Stack                         |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `frontend/`      | Web UI                                        | React 18 + Vite (npm)         |
| `backend/`       | HTTP API                                      | Node + Express + Prisma (npm) |
| `engine/`        | Scan worker running the AI harnesses          | Python 3.11+ (Ruff)           |
| `database/`      | Postgres image + `init/*.sql` migrations      | Postgres 16                   |
| `executor-view/` | Executor viewer                               | Python                        |
| `scripts/`       | Repo tooling and CLI implementation           | Node                          |

The whole product ships as **one version** — the repo-root [`VERSION`](VERSION) file.

## Run / build / test

Fastest full stack: `cp .env.example .env && docker compose up --build`
(add `-f docker-compose.dev.yml` for human-readable backend logs).

For guided local onboarding, run `./kritt` for the full-screen Arrow-key menu, or use
`./kritt setup` and `./kritt start` directly (Node.js 20+ required; no npm install needed
for the CLI).

Per component:

```bash
# frontend
cd frontend && npm install
npm run dev | npm run build | npm run lint | npm run format | npm test   # Vitest

# backend  (needs DATABASE_URL; see .env.example)
cd backend && npm install
npx prisma generate && npm run migrate     # apply database/init/*.sql (idempotent)
npm run dev | npm run lint | npm run format | npm test                   # node:test

# engine
cd engine && pip install -r requirements.txt
ruff check . | ruff format . | pytest
python -m open_kritt_engine                # run the worker
```

## House rules (do)

- **Keep changes focused.** Keep unrelated edits out of the diff; add or update tests
  and documentation whenever behavior or configuration changes.
- **Conventional Commits** for every commit: `feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `refactor:`,
  `test:`, `chore:`, `ci:`. Scope is optional (`feat(frontend): …`), but an empty
  scope is invalid: use `feat:` or `feat(frontend):`, never `feat():`. Mark breaking
  changes with `!` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer. Release effects are:
  - `feat` → minor release (patch while the project is pre-1.0)
  - `fix` → patch release
  - breaking change → minor release while pre-1.0
  - `docs`, `chore`, `refactor`, `test`, `ci` → no release on their own
- **Lint & format before proposing changes** (ESLint/Prettier for JS, Ruff for
  Python). Match the existing style; don't reformat unrelated code.
- **Never commit secrets or local data:** credentials, tokens, `.env`, provider login
  data, or scan outputs. Use the provided `gitleaks` pre-commit hook.
- **DB changes are additive, idempotent, forward-only**: a new
  `database/init/NNN_*.sql` using `CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS` / `ADD COLUMN IF NOT
  EXISTS`, then update `backend/prisma/schema.prisma` to match and run the migration
  twice. CI also runs `migrate.js` twice to prove idempotency.
- **One version, one source of truth**: normal contributions do not bump versions. If
  a manual version change is explicitly required, change [`VERSION`](VERSION), then
  run `node scripts/sync-version.mjs`. Never hand-edit a component's version.
- **Pin Docker image tags** (never `:latest`).

## Contribution workflow

Before starting:

- Search existing issues before filing a bug or feature request.
- Use GitHub Discussions for questions, ideas, and larger proposals to avoid
  duplicated work.
- Never report a vulnerability publicly. Use the private reporting flow in
  [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md); if that is unavailable, open a public issue containing
  no vulnerability details and ask for a private channel.
- External contributors should fork the repository and work on a branch. Branch names
  such as `feat/my-change` are examples, not a required naming scheme.

Before proposing a change, run the checks for every area touched:

| Area | Required local checks |
| ---- | --------------------- |
| Frontend | `cd frontend && npm install && npm run lint && npm run format:check && npm test && npm run build` |
| Backend | `cd backend && npm install && npx prisma generate && npx prisma validate && npm run lint && npm run format:check && npm test` |
| Engine | `cd engine && pip install -r requirements.txt && ruff check . && ruff format --check . && pytest` |
| CLI | `node --test scripts/kritt.test.mjs scripts/kritt-ui.test.mjs scripts/kritt-headless.test.mjs` |
| Documentation | `cd docs-site && npm run check-links` |

Engine tests are currently local-only; CI does not run them. For changes crossing
component boundaries, also run the recommended full-stack smoke test:

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

Open pull requests against `main`. Keep them small and complete the pull request
template: explain what changed and why, link the related issue (for example,
`Closes #123`), identify the change type and affected components, list checks run,
include screenshots for visible UI changes, call out breaking changes, and leave useful
reviewer notes. The PR type should match the Conventional Commit type. CI must pass
before merge.

The repository provides optional pre-commit automation:

```bash

pre-commit install
pre-commit run --all-files
```

It checks common file hygiene, merge-conflict markers, files over 512 KiB, YAML/JSON,

Any intentional authenticated submission for inclusion in the official repository —

## Gotchas (don't get bitten)

- **Prisma engine is platform-specific.** A `node_modules` generated on macOS won't
  run Prisma on Linux (and vice-versa). Don't run backend/DB code against a client
  built for another OS; regenerate with `npx prisma generate` on the target platform.
- **Frontend native optional dependencies.** Rollup and esbuild ship separate
  packages per OS, architecture, and libc. Regenerate `frontend/package-lock.json`
  only from a clean dependency graph (no old lockfile or `node_modules`) so npm
  records every platform package. CI runs both `npm ci` and an Alpine/musl image
  smoke test to catch a platform-pruned lockfile.
- **Frontend version at build time** comes from `frontend/package.json` (kept in sync
  with `VERSION`), NOT `../VERSION` — the repo root isn't in the frontend Docker image.

- **Reserved key patterns** in scan/enrichment results are meaningful, not arbitrary:

- **This is a security tool.** It runs AI agents over untrusted code and holds provider
  API keys / `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Never commit secrets (a `gitleaks` pre-commit hook helps),

## Technical Reference

### Codex Compatibility

This repository uses Claude plugin marketplace metadata as the canonical source for Claude Code, Codex, and ChatGPT workspace imports. Codex supports `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and `plugins/<name>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` directly, so do not add duplicate Codex-only sidecar metadata.

Rules:

- Do not add `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, `.codex/`, `.opencode/`, or
  `plugins/<name>/.codex-plugin/`. The validator enforces this — sidecars drift out of
  sync with the canonical metadata, which is why the last set was removed in #173.
- Keep plugin components at the plugin root using Codex-compatible default paths: `skills/`, `hooks/hooks.json`, `.mcp.json`, and `.app.json`.
- Skill interfaces in `skills/<skill>/agents/openai.yaml` use snake_case: when that optional file
  exists, `interface.display_name` and `interface.short_description` must both be
  non-empty strings. OpenAI documents these requirements and their error messages in
  [Skill agent metadata errors](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/deploy/submission-errors#skill-agent-metadata-errors).
  An icon-only file fails these requirements.
  `validate_skill_interfaces.py` checks these files in `make check`, pre-commit, and
  the Python tests job in `lint.yml`, which already installs PyYAML.
- Omit unknown optional author contacts instead of setting `email` or `url` to `""`.
- If a plugin needs MCP configuration, put it in `.mcp.json` at the plugin root rather than embedding an object in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`.
- Both loadability checks run in CI, not in `make check` — they need the Claude Code
  and Codex CLIs installed, which is not a reasonable local prerequisite. Run them by
  hand if you are changing plugin metadata:

  ```sh
  python3 .github/scripts/check_claude_loadability.py
  python3 .github/scripts/check_codex_loadability.py
  ```

  If one fails, update the canonical Claude marketplace or the plugin root components
  so Codex can load them through Claude marketplace compatibility — do not add a
  sidecar to work around it.

### Plugin Structure

```
plugins/
  <plugin-name>/
    .claude-plugin/
      plugin.json         # Plugin metadata (name, version, description, author)
    commands/             # Optional: slash commands
    agents/               # Optional: autonomous agents
    workflows/            # Optional: dynamic workflows (*.js), ships as /<plugin>:<workflow>
    evals/                # Optional: `claude plugin eval` cases + graders
    skills/               # Optional: knowledge/guidance
      <skill-name>/
        SKILL.md          # Entry point with frontmatter
        references/       # Optional: detailed docs
        workflows/        # Optional: step-by-step guides (prose, not scripts)
        scripts/          # Optional: utility scripts
    hooks/                # Optional: event hooks
    tests/                # Optional: run_*.sh suites (CI runs these — keep them free)
    README.md             # Plugin documentation
```

**Important**: Component directories (`skills/`, `commands/`, `agents/`, `hooks/`) must be at the plugin root, NOT inside `.claude-plugin/`. Only `plugin.json` belongs in `.claude-plugin/`.

**Two different `workflows/`.** A **dynamic workflow** is a JavaScript file at the *plugin
root* under `workflows/`; it exports a `meta` object, orchestrates subagents in code, and
ships through the marketplace as `/<plugin-name>:<workflow-name>` (from `meta.name`, not the
filename). The older `skills/<skill>/workflows/` holds prose step-by-step guides. If a
SKILL.md has "Phase 1", "for each finding", or "repeat until" sections, the plan belongs in
a script at the plugin root, not in prose. See `plugins/variant-analysis/workflows/` for a
worked example, and note that `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is **not** available inside a workflow
script — it is not a hook, MCP, or LSP subprocess.

### Frontmatter

Skills and commands declare tools with `allowed-tools`, space-delimited:

```yaml
---
name: skill-name              # kebab-case, max 64 chars
description: "Third-person description of what it does and when to use it"
allowed-tools: Read Grep      # Optional: restrict to needed tools only
---
```

Agent files under `agents/` use a different key — `tools`, as a YAML list:

```yaml
---
name: agent-name
description: "What this agent does and when the coordinator should dispatch it"
tools:
  - Read
  - Grep
---
```

The keys are inverted between the two file types, and the loader silently ignores
the wrong one — the frontmatter still parses, the restriction simply does not apply
and the agent inherits everything. The validator checks this.

### Naming Conventions

- **kebab-case**: `constant-time-analysis`, not `constantTimeAnalysis`
- **Gerund form preferred**: `analyzing-contracts`, `processing-pdfs` (not `contract-analyzer`, `pdf-processor`)
- **Avoid vague names**: `helper`, `utils`, `tools`, `misc`
- **Avoid reserved words**: `anthropic`, `claude`

### Path Handling

- Use `{baseDir}` for paths, **never hardcode** absolute paths
- Use forward slashes (`/`) even on Windows

### Python Scripts

When skills include Python scripts with dependencies:

1. **Use PEP 723 inline metadata** - Declare dependencies in the script header:
   ```python
   # /// script
   # requires-python = ">=3.11"
   # dependencies = ["requests>=2.28", "pydantic>=2.0"]
   # ///
   ```

2. **Use `uv run`** - Enables automatic dependency resolution:
   ```bash
   uv run {baseDir}/scripts/process.py input.pdf
   ```

3. **Include `pyproject.toml`** - Keep in `scripts/` for development tooling (ruff, etc.)

4. **Document system dependencies** - List non-Python deps (poppler, tesseract) in workflows with platform-specific install commands

### Hooks

PreToolUse hooks run on every Bash command—performance is critical:

- **Prefer shell + jq** over Python—interpreter startup (Python + tree-sitter) adds noticeable latency
- **Fast-fail early** - exit 0 immediately for non-matching commands so most invocations are instant
- **Favor regex over AST parsing** - accept rare false positives if performance gain is significant and Claude can rephrase
- **Anticipate false positive patterns** - diagnostic commands (`which python`), search tools (`grep python`), and filenames (`cat python.txt`) shouldn't trigger interception
- **Document tradeoffs** in PR descriptions so reviewers understand deliberate design choices

## Quality Standards

These are Trail of Bits house standards on top of Anthropic's requirements.

### Description Quality

Your skill competes with 100+ others. The description must trigger correctly.

- **Third-person voice**: "Analyzes X" not "I help with X"
- **Include triggers**: "Use when auditing Solidity" not just "Smart contract tool"
- **Be specific**: "Detects reentrancy vulnerabilities" not "Helps with security"

### Value-Add

Skills should provide guidance Claude doesn't already have, not duplicate reference material.

- **Behavioral guidance over reference dumps** - Don't paste entire specs; teach when and how to look things up
- **Explain WHY, not just WHAT** - Include trade-offs, decision criteria, judgment calls
- **Document anti-patterns WITH explanations** - Say why something is wrong, not just that it's wrong

**Example**: The DWARF skill doesn't include the full DWARF spec. It teaches Claude how to use `dwarfdump`, `readelf`, and `pyelftools` to look up what it needs, plus judgment about when each tool is appropriate.

### Scope Boundaries

Prescriptiveness should match task risk:
- **Strict for fragile tasks** - Security audits, crypto implementations, compliance checks need rigid step-by-step enforcement
- **Flexible for variable tasks** - Code exploration, documentation, refactoring can offer options and judgment calls

### Security Skills

For audit/security skills, also include:

```markdown
## Rationalizations to Reject
[Common shortcuts or rationalizations that lead to missed findings]
```

### Content Organization

- Keep SKILL.md **under 500 lines** - split into `references/`, `workflows/`
- Use **progressive disclosure** - quick start first, details in linked files
- **One level deep** - SKILL.md links to files, files don't chain to more files

Note: Directory depth is fine (`references/guides/topic.md`). Reference *chains* are not (`SKILL.md → file1.md → file2.md` where file1 references file2). The problem is chained references, not nested folders.

### Progressive Disclosure Pattern

```markdown
## Quick Start
[Core instructions here]

## Advanced Usage
See [ADVANCED.md](references/ADVANCED.md) for detailed patterns.

## API Reference
See [API.md](references/API.md) for complete method documentation.
```

## Before committing

```sh
make check
```

That runs the plugin metadata and skill interface validator self-tests, the
eval-harness self-tests, ruff, shellcheck, shfmt, bats, the plugin Python suites,
the plugin `*.test.mjs` suites, and both validators.

It needs `uv`, `shellcheck`, `shfmt`, `bats`, and `node` on PATH. `node` is the newest
of those and the one most likely to be missing — without it `make check` stops at
`js-tests` with a bare `node: command not found`.

It is most of CI, not all of it. Additional checks run in CI, so a green `make check`
is strong evidence and not a guarantee:

- **the two loadability checks**, which need the Claude Code and Codex CLIs installed
- **review-walkthrough's browser checks**, which need Chrome or Chromium. Run
  `node plugins/review-walkthrough/tests/browser-check.mjs /path/to/chromium` locally.
- **the rest of pre-commit** — actionlint, zizmor, check-yaml/json/toml,
  detect-private-key, end-of-file-fixer, trailing-whitespace. Run `prek run -a` (or
  `pre-commit run -a`) to cover those locally.
- **the version-increment check**, which needs a base ref to diff against and so has
  no meaning outside a PR.
- **`make shell-suites`**, a target but not part of `check` — slow, not broken. It passes
  with modern-python ≥ 1.6.0 installed; the 1.5.3 shim still refuses the `python3 -` that
  zeroize-audit's suite uses.

Both scan every plugin; the validator is not scoped down in CI. Only the
version-increment check is limited to the plugins a branch touched, and it is the one
check CI runs that local cannot. Do not add a scoping flag to the local run — the
zero-reference guard only arms on a full scan.

`make fix` applies the formatting CI would otherwise reject. `make help` lists the rest.

### What the validator enforces, so you do not have to

Each of these fails the build. There is no value in checking any of it by hand:

- `plugin.json` exists, parses, and has `name`, `description`, and a semver `version`
- `plugin.json`'s `name` equals the plugin's directory name
- Plugin directory name is kebab-case and ≤64 characters
- Plugin has a `README.md` (exact case — `Readme.md` passes on macOS and fails on CI)
- Registered in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, the root `README.md`, and `CODEOWNERS`
- The marketplace entry's `source` is exactly `./plugins/<name>` and its `description`
  matches `plugin.json`
- `version` matches between `plugin.json` and `marketplace.json`, **and** increases when
  you change a plugin — clients only pull an update when the number goes up, so a fix
  shipped without a bump reaches nobody. Apply the `no-version-bump` label for
  typo-only changes and CI skips the check.
- `SKILL.md` has frontmatter, and no top-level value is an unquoted YAML scalar
  containing `: ` or ` #`. Either one makes the whole block unparseable, and the
  loader then drops *every* field and loads the skill with empty metadata — so a
  skill whose `description:` line reads perfectly well ships with no description
  and never triggers. Quote any description containing a colon.
- Agent files use `tools:`; skills and commands use `allowed-tools:`
- `subagent_type` values are namespaced `<plugin>:<agent>` — a bare name is
  unregistered and the dispatch fails at runtime, whether it names this plugin's own
  agent, another plugin's, or nothing at all
- A plugin's `README.md` names every skill, agent, command, and dynamic workflow it
  ships. A reader cannot invoke what is not written down, and the gap is worst where
  it is least guessable — a skill whose name is not the plugin name, or a workflow,
  which ships under its `meta.name` rather than its filename. Commands and workflows
  must appear in the `/<plugin>:<name>` form, since that is the only string a user can
  type; agents must appear as an identifier (backticked, an `agents/<name>` path, or
  namespaced), because a bare word in a sentence is not a dispatchable name; skills
  need only a delimited mention.
- No hardcoded `/Users/…` or `/home/…` paths, in any `.md`, `.py`, `.json`, `.sh`,
  `.bats`, `.yml` or `.toml` file under `plugins/`. `*-shim.bats` is exempt because
  those fixtures need literal paths, and `/path/to` and `/home/vscode` are treated as
  placeholders rather than somebody's home directory.
- No documented command uses a form the `modern-python` shims refuse: `python <script>`,
  `pip install`, `python -m pip`, or `uv pip install` without `--project`/`--directory`/
  `--target`/`-t`. Use `uv run --no-project <script>`, `uv run --with <pkg>`, `uv add`, or
  `uv tool install`. Exempt: prose forbidding the command, `dockerfile` fences,
  `plugins/modern-python/` itself, `.md`/`.py` under a `tests`/`evals*` directory (quoted
  expectations), and code blocks carrying `allow-legacy-python: <reason>` — the reason is
  required.
- No `.codex/`, `.opencode/`, `.agents/`, or `plugins/*/.codex-plugin/` sidecars
- A committed `uv.lock` for every uv directory listed in `.github/dependabot.yml`
- Both loadability checks pass under the real Claude Code and Codex CLIs

Two more are reported as **warnings**, so they will not stop a merge and do still
need your eye: `SKILL.md` over 500 lines, and references that do not resolve. A dangling
`references/setup.md` link 404s for every user of the skill, and CI will not stop you
shipping it.

### What no tool can check — this is the part that needs you

- **The description actually triggers.** Third person, names the situation, uses the
  words a user would actually type. This is the single highest-leverage line in a skill:
  a skill that never triggers may as well not exist.
- **Examples are concrete** — real input, real output, not a shape.
- **It explains why**, including the trade-off and when not to do the thing.
- **The version bump is the right size.** The validator confirms the number went up;
  only you know whether the change was substantive. `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, MINOR for
  features, PATCH for fixes.
- **CODEOWNERS lists the right people**: `/plugins/<name>/ @you @dguido`. Find your
  username with `gh api user --jq .login`.
- **The entry is in the right section** of the root `README.md`. The validator only
  checks that the plugin appears *somewhere* in that file, so a row appended to
  whichever table you scrolled to first passes CI and stays filed under the wrong
  category indefinitely.

## Scripts a plugin ships

**A checker that inspects zero items must fail, not pass.** This is the single most
expensive class of bug in a repo like this one, because it is invisible on every read
and in every review. Real examples, all of which were green for months:

- a validator using `grep -oP` (rejected by BSD grep) with stderr sent to `/dev/null`,
  so it printed "all valid" on every run without ever matching anything
- an eval grader that judged the response text rather than the artifact, so a run that
  skipped the actual work still scored a pass
- a citation gate that validated only the citations that were present, so a document
  with zero citations passed

If your script counts, filters, or matches, make it exit non-zero when the count is
zero, and give it a fixture proving it still detects its target. The validator's
`--self-test` is the worked example: it builds a known-bad plugin in a tempdir and
asserts each checker rejects it, and it fails if it runs fewer assertions than it
should — because the self-test is itself a checker.

Otherwise: `set -euo pipefail`, POSIX ERE rather than PCRE (`grep -oP` is not portable
to macOS), and never send a tool's stderr to `/dev/null` unless you have handled the
failure it would have reported.

## Working effectively in this repo

- **Effort.** Start at `xhigh` for coding and agentic work and `high` elsewhere, then
  sweep downward on your own evals — `low` and `medium` are unusually strong on current
  models and often match what an older model needed `xhigh` to do. Defaults carried over
  from a previous model are rarely the right setting.
- **Subagents.** Delegate work that is large and genuinely independent — a wide
  multi-file investigation, several unrelated tracks. Do not spawn subagents to verify
  or double-check your own work, and do not split one modest job across several: each
  one re-establishes context, re-explores, and reports back, and then you re-read the
  report. One well-briefed agent beats three vague ones.
- **Do not add verification scaffolding to prompts.** "Double-check your answer", "add a
  final verification step", and similar make output worse on current models rather than
  better — they cause over-verification, and removing them costs no capability. This
  inverts older advice, so it is worth stating explicitly. Put the check in `make check`
  or the validator, where it runs deterministically and cannot be talked out of firing.
  This applies to skills you write or edit; existing skills carrying the pattern are not
  a cleanup backlog, so strip it when you are already in the file rather than as its own
  sweep.
- **Do not tell a reviewer to pre-filter.** "Only report high-severity issues" is
  followed literally: the model investigates just as thoroughly, finds the bugs, and
  then declines to report what it judges below the bar. Precision rises, recall appears
  to collapse, and the regression looks like a capability problem when it is a prompt
  problem. Ask for everything with a severity attached and filter in a separate pass —
  `c-review` and `rust-review` do this correctly if you want a model to copy.

===== verify-delivery.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read-only evidence verification; writes no sealed campaign artifacts."""
from pathlib import Path
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
issues = []
checked = {}

def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()

def check(path, expected, label):
    if not path.is_file():
        issues.append(f"Missing {label}: {path}")
    elif sha(path) != expected:
        issues.append(f"Hash mismatch {label}: {path}")

freeze = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(root / "verify-freeze.py")], capture_output=True, text=True)
try:
    checked["freeze"] = json.loads(freeze.stdout)
except json.JSONDecodeError:
    issues.append("Freeze verifier did not return JSON")
if freeze.returncode:
    issues.append("Frozen inputs differ")

matrix = json.loads((root / "matrix.json").read_text())
ids = [row["id"] for row in matrix["runs"]]
if len(ids) != len(set(ids)):
    issues.append("Duplicate matrix IDs")
required = {f"{provider}-{method}" for provider in ["OPENAI", "CLAUDE", "GEMINI"] for method in ["SIMAO", "PASHOV", "OPENKRITT", "TOB", "GEBAL"]}
if not required.issubset(ids):
    issues.append("Required fifteen-cell matrix is missing entries")
expected = required | {f"DAYBREAK-{method}" for method in ["SIMAO", "PASHOV", "OPENKRITT", "TOB", "GEBAL"]} | {"SUP-A1", "SUP-A2", "SUP-S1"}
if not expected.issubset(ids):
    issues.append("Daybreak or supplementary matrix entries are missing")
unfinished = []
for row in matrix["runs"]:
    if row["id"] not in expected:
        continue
    # Only an actual OpenAI refusal satisfies the user's stop condition.
    # Other providers' failed original attempts require a completed, disclosed
    # continuation; setup failures and arbitrary time budgets are not terminal.
    allowed_refusal = row.get("provider") == "OPENAI" and row.get("execution_state") == "PROVIDER_REJECTED"
    continuation = row.get("continuation", {})
    completed_variant = continuation.get("state") == "COMPLETE" and bool(continuation.get("completion_receipt"))
    if row.get("workflow_status") != "COMPLETE" and not allowed_refusal and not completed_variant:
        unfinished.append(row["id"])
    if continuation.get("state") == "RUNNING":
        unfinished.append(row["id"] + " qualified continuation")
if "--require-terminal" in sys.argv and unfinished:
    issues.append("Eligible requested work is unfinished: " + ", ".join(unfinished))
checked["required_cells_present"] = len(required.intersection(ids))
checked["total_matrix_rows"] = len(ids)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Seal or read-only verify the completed, quiescent audit delivery package."""
from pathlib import Path
import argparse
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
EXCLUDED = {"DELIVERY-MANIFEST.json", "DELIVERY-SEAL.json"}


def digest(path):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as stream:
        for block in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            h.update(block)
    return h.hexdigest()


def inventory():
    result = {}
    for directory, subdirs, files in os.walk(ROOT, followlinks=False):
        base = Path(directory)
        names = files + [name for name in subdirs if (base / name).is_symlink()]
        for name in sorted(names):
            path = base / name
            relative = path.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
            if relative in EXCLUDED:
                continue
            before = path.lstat()
            if path.is_symlink():
                row = {"kind": "symlink", "target": os.readlink(path)}
            elif path.is_file():
                row = {"kind": "file", "bytes": before.st_size, "sha256": digest(path)}
            else:
                raise RuntimeError(f"Unsupported package object: {relative}")
            after = path.lstat()
            if (before.st_ino, before.st_size, before.st_mtime_ns) != (after.st_ino, after.st_size, after.st_mtime_ns):
                raise RuntimeError(f"Package changed during hashing: {relative}")
            result[relative] = row
    return dict(sorted(result.items()))


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--seal", action="store_true", help="Create a final seal once; refuses existing seals and unfinished lanes")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    manifest_path = ROOT / "DELIVERY-MANIFEST.json"
    seal_path = ROOT / "DELIVERY-SEAL.json"
    if args.seal:
        if manifest_path.exists() or seal_path.exists():
            raise RuntimeError("Delivery already sealed; preserve the original and use a new named addendum")
        run = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ROOT / "verify-delivery.py"), "--require-terminal"], capture_output=True, text=True)
        if run.returncode:
            sys.stdout.write(run.stdout)
            sys.stderr.write(run.stderr)
            raise RuntimeError("Delivery integrity or required terminal-state check failed")
        (ROOT / "FINAL-VERIFICATION.json").write_text(run.stdout)
        rows = inventory()
        # A second walk catches additions, removals and concurrent log changes.
        if rows != inventory():
            raise RuntimeError("Package is still changing; quiesce owned writers before sealing")
        manifest = {
            "schema": "raffle-audit-delivery-manifest/v1",
            "created_at": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(),
            "excluded_self_references": sorted(EXCLUDED),
            "symlink_policy": "Link text is bound; external target bytes are not embedded by this manifest. Frozen inputs and separately retained artifacts have their own manifests.",
            "files": rows,
        }
        manifest_path.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + "\n")
        seal = {
            "schema": "raffle-audit-delivery-seal/v1",
            "sealed_at": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(),
            "target": json.loads((ROOT / "freeze.json").read_text())["head"],
            "manifest": manifest_path.name,
            "manifest_sha256": digest(manifest_path),
            "report": "FINAL-AUDIT-REPORT.md",
            "report_sha256": digest(ROOT / "FINAL-AUDIT-REPORT.md"),
            "verification": "FINAL-VERIFICATION.json",
            "verification_sha256": digest(ROOT / "FINAL-VERIFICATION.json"),
            "regular_files": sum(row["kind"] == "file" for row in rows.values()),
            "symlinks": sum(row["kind"] == "symlink" for row in rows.values()),
            "interpretation": "Tamper-evident byte binding, not WORM storage, external auditor certification or release approval.",
        }
        seal_path.write_text(json.dumps(seal, indent=2) + "\n")
        print(json.dumps(seal, indent=2))
    else:
        seal = json.loads(seal_path.read_text())
        if digest(manifest_path) != seal["manifest_sha256"]:
            raise RuntimeError("Delivery manifest hash mismatch")
        expected = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text())["files"]
        actual = inventory()
        missing = sorted(set(expected) - set(actual))
        added = sorted(set(actual) - set(expected))
        changed = sorted(name for name in expected.keys() & actual.keys() if expected[name] != actual[name])
        result = {"ok": not (missing or added or changed), "checked_objects": len(expected), "missing": missing, "added": added, "changed": changed}
        print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
        return 0 if result["ok"] else 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

item.aggregated_output:
===== CLAUDE-TOB/S6/attempt-02/final-result.md =====
I ran the complete five-step workflow on all five production files. The full report is at `TOB-S6-secure-workflow-guide.md` in the work directory. The headline is no critical or code-level fund-loss bug within the bounded analysis, plus two Medium design-level risks that should be settled before deployment. Everything ran offline in disclosed scratch copies. The original inputs, including `packages/contracts/foundry.toml`, are byte-identical to the pre-run baseline.

**Results by step**
- **Step 1, Slither** (`slither . --exclude-dependencies`, 102 detectors):
  - Production code has 0 High, 0 Medium and 14 Low/Informational results. All 14 are triaged, as are the one Medium suppressed by an inline comment and the High/Medium results in dependencies.
  - The calls-loop result is a false positive, confirmed by a test showing one registry lookup per refund transaction rather than one per ticket.
- **Step 2, special features:**
  - The ticket is fully ERC-721/ERC-165 conformant.
  - The clone and one-time initializer pattern passes the upgradeability checks, with Informational results only.
  - `slither-prop` doesn't apply (confirmed by search and by the tool itself); `token-integration-analyzer` is recommended.
- **Step 3, diagrams:** all three printers were run, rendered to SVG/PNG, and reviewed. Slither 0.11.6's inheritance-graph printer drops a real edge when interfaces are hidden; I documented this and used the `--include-interfaces` output instead.
- **Step 4, properties and testing.** 45 properties are documented. Within the bounds, none was violated:

  | Campaign | Size | Result |
  |---|---|---|
  | Echidna, property mode | 400,073 calls | 9/9 invariants pass |
  | Echidna, assertion mode | 400,047 calls | 38/38 pass |
  | Medusa | 3,116,102 calls | 46/46 pass |
  | Foundry | 20 tests | 20/20 pass |
  | Custom Slither checks | 12 checks | 12/12 pass |
  | Halmos (symbolic) | 9 checks | 7 pass, 2 undecided |

  - Halmos is standing in for Manticore, which isn't installed and couldn't be installed offline.
  - The two undecided checks are the fee split and refund conservation. Three solver attempts timed out without finding a counterexample: Halmos's default solver at 10 minutes, z3 at 30, and 32-bit bounded variants at 20. Those two properties rest on full-range fuzzing plus a short hand derivation in the report.
  - Two bugs in my own test harness came up and were fixed before the bounded campaigns; both are preserved in the evidence.

**Findings (Step 5)**

| ID | Severity | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| S6-F5 | Medium | A sponsor can push a raffle over its reserve just before the sale ends, at about 5% of the shortfall. In the measured case this flips the outcome from cash to NFT: the sponsor's net payout goes from 135 to 850 USDC, and buyers lose a 720 USDC cash prize. |
| S6-F2 | Medium | The sponsor is paid whether or not the NFT can actually be delivered. A pausable or sponsor-controlled collection lets them take 95% while the winner can never redeem. |
| S6-F1 | Low | Tickets stay tradeable while the random result is visible in the mempool but not yet on-chain. |
| S6-F3 | Low | Escrow verification trusts the prize contract, so a dishonest one can create a raffle with no real prize held. |
| S6-F4, F6, F7, F8 | Informational | See report. |

Every Medium and Low finding, plus F4, has a passing test that reproduces it against the unmodified code. The report also includes a prioritized action plan with effort estimates and a checklist.

**Identity:** model `claude-opus-5-5`. Local effort was max; applied server effort is recorded as unknown because it wasn't echoed. No subagents were used and no provider refusal occurred. The skill is pinned at commit `82fe8226`.

**Remaining gaps:**
- USDC, the Chainlink VRF wrapper and the prize NFTs were mocked; no fork test was possible without network access.
- The fuzzing harness handles at most 2 raffles and 4 users.
- The 100-ticket refund cap and the defensive `PrizeDeliveryVerificationFailed`/`PrizeEscrowVerificationFailed` branches were never triggered.
- The solc binary's hash couldn't be checked against the official release list offline.
- Frontend, deployment scripts and `slither.config.json` weren't provided.

**Where things are** (in the work directory):
- `evidence/01-slither/09-slither-triage.md` — Slither triage
- `evidence/02-special-features/09-step2-summary.md` — special-feature checks
- `evidence/03-visual/png/` — diagrams, with review notes in `09-diagram-review.md`
- `evidence/04-properties/00-security-properties.md` — properties; campaign logs `40-`, `41-`, `51-`, `60-`
- `evidence/05-manual/01-manual-review.md` — manual review
- `evidence/99-integrity/final-integrity-check.txt` — integrity check
- `_generated/` — all generated test code and scripts

## Executive summary

The complete five-step workflow ran offline on all five mandatory production files, with every raw command and result
preserved. The original inputs stayed byte-identical: verified by hash at baseline, mid-run and at the end (§0.4).

- **Step 1 — Slither.** No High or Medium results in production code. All 14 Low/Informational results and the one
  inline-suppressed Medium are triaged with file:line and evidence. The `calls-loop` result is a false positive, proven at
  runtime. Dependency High/Medium results are known OpenZeppelin false positives or unreachable Chainlink code.
- **Step 2 — Special features.**
  - The ticket is **fully ERC-721/ERC-165 conformant**.
  - The ERC-1167 clone and one-shot initializer pattern passes the upgradeability checks (Informational only), including
    against a generated 1167 proxy model.
  - There is no upgrade path.
  - `slither-prop` does not apply (verified by search and by the tool); `token-integration-analyzer` is recommended.
- **Step 3 — Diagrams.** All three generated, rendered (SVG/PNG) and reviewed. They confirm clone-safe constructors,
  `nonReentrant` on every value-moving entry point, and only four authorization roles. A Slither printer defect was found
  and worked around.
- **Step 4 — Properties and testing.** 45 security properties are documented and encoded in runnable generated
  infrastructure. Within the bounds, **no property was violated**:
  - Echidna property and assertion modes (2 × 400k calls);
  - Medusa (3.1M calls);
  - 20 Foundry tests, including 2 × 2,000 full-domain fuzz runs;
  - 9 Halmos checks;
  - 12 custom Slither checks.

  Halmos verified 7 of 9 checks over all inputs within its bounds. The 2 arithmetic-heavy checks hit solver timeouts
  (unknown, no counterexample). Two follow-ups also ended undecided: z3 run directly on the saved queries (30 min each) and uint32-bounded variants (20 min each). These two properties therefore rest on the full-domain concrete fuzzing and the short hand derivation in 4.3, not on a symbolic result.
- **Step 5 — Manual review.** The core accounting and state machine held up. The material risks sit in the economic and
  trust model:
  - **S6-F5 (Medium):** a sponsor-controlled purchase just before `endTime` flips a cash raffle into an NFT raffle for
    about 5% of the reserve shortfall. Measured: the sponsor's USDC payout rises from 135 to 850 net, and buyers lose a
    720 USDC cash prize.
  - **S6-F2 (Medium):** sponsor proceeds don't depend on the NFT being deliverable. A sponsor-controlled or pausable
    collection lets the sponsor take 95% while the winner can never redeem.
  - **S6-F1 (Low):** tickets stay tradeable while the VRF answer is visible but not yet included.
  - **S6-F3 (Low):** escrow verification trusts the prize contract.
  - **S6-F4, S6-F6, S6-F7, S6-F8:** Informational.

**Bottom line:** no critical issue and no code-level fund-loss bug was found within the bounded analysis. Before
deployment, the project should settle the S6-F5 and S6-F2 design questions and decide on S6-F1 (see Action plan).

  (`initialized=true`, `status=Refunding`, dead ERC721 name strings, a reentrancy slot whose 0 value is safe). All clone
  state comes from the factory's atomic `initialize`.
- Every value-moving/untrusted-calling Raffle entry point is `nonReentrant`; the only roles are factory (init), VRF
  wrapper (callback), sponsor (close an EMPTY raffle) and ticket owners (redeem/refund).
- Two diagram-driven leads for Step 5: the transfer hook gates destinations but not lifecycle state (→ S6-F1), and
  sponsor proceeds are allocated/released independently of NFT deliverability (→ S6-F2); outcome type depends only on
  `totalEntries` vs `reserveEntries` (→ S6-F5).

## Step 4 — Document security properties and set up testing

### 4.1 Properties (independently derived)

Full catalogue with source anchors and test mapping: **`evidence/04-properties/00-security-properties.md`** —
12 state-machine (SM-1…12), 9 accounting (A-1…9), 5 ticket-ledger (T-1…5), 7 access-control (AC-1…7), 4 arithmetic
(AR-1…4), 5 external-interaction (EI-1…5) and 3 standards (ST-1…3) properties. Core invariants:

1. **Exact solvency/conservation:** `USDC.balanceOf(raffle) == accountedQuoteBalance() + donations` and
   `paidOut + accountedQuoteBalance() == totalEntries × 1e6` (accounting never reads balances).
2. **Lifecycle:** only `AwaitingPrize→Active→{Drawing|Refunding}`, `Drawing→{NftWon|CashWon|Refunding}`; terminal
   states absorbing; windows `[endTime, endTime+2d)` (request), `< drawRequestedAt+2d` (callback), refunds at the
   deadlines — disjoint at every boundary.
3. **Split exactness:** fee ⌊5%⌋, cash ⌊80%⌋, sponsor remainder; fee+cash+sponsor == gross; exact for 1e6-unit entries.
4. **Ticket ledger:** ranges partition `[1,totalEntries]`; refund liability = price × live entries; no ticket owned
   by protocol plumbing.
5. **Prize custody:** escrowed until exactly one release (winner in NftWon; `sponsorRecipient` in CashWon/Refunding).
6. **Callback liveness:** authenticated callbacks never revert, use ≪ 300k gas, and resolve only when valid.
