## Canonical final findings register

### DAYBREAK-F-01 — Critical — An untrusted prize can fake escrow and delivery while buyer-funded proceeds are released

**Confidence:** High.

**Affected code and functions:**

- [`RaffleFactory.createRaffle`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol:97), including prize transfer/postconditions at lines 127–147.
- [`RaffleFactory._validateCreateParams`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol:154).
- [`Raffle.onERC721Received`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:416).
- Prize delivery, settlement, and releases in [`Raffle.sol`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:304).
- Conflicting trust statement in [`IRaffle.sol`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/interfaces/IRaffle.sol:12).

**Lineage:** S3 H-01 and L-01; S4 S4-SEC-01; S5 F-01 covering REQ-14, REQ-48, and REQ-53; source-first `FP-SEC-01`; S6-01.

**Dynamic status:** Confirmed. `test_Evidence_MaliciousPrizeCanFakeEscrowAndDelivery` completed creation, purchase, draw, settlement, sponsor and treasury release, and purported delivery. The buyer became the prize’s reported owner while the mock’s separate actual owner remained the malicious sponsor. The desired negative property failed intentionally.

**Exploit and preconditions:** A malicious sponsor selects a contract that reports ERC-721 support, invokes the expected receiver callback without transferring a genuine asset, and lies through `ownerOf`. Entrants then pay real quote tokens. With a trivially met reserve, the raffle reaches `NftWon`; 95% can be released to the sponsor recipient and 5% to treasury before trustworthy prize delivery exists. The token may later revert forever or fabricate successful delivery.

**Impact:** Direct, source-uncapped buyer loss and fraudulent raffle publication. There is no `NftWon` transition to refunds after proceeds have been released.

**Severity adjudication:** S3, S4, and S6 rated the issue High; S5 and the sealed source-first synthesis rated it Critical. The final rating is **Critical** because S6 confirmed the complete buyer-loss and proceeds-release sequence, while source imposes no pot cap. The malicious-sponsor and entrant-participation preconditions are retained rather than hidden.

**Remediation direction:**

- Enforce a deployment-specific allowlist or attested immutable collection registry, including upgrade/admin provenance.
- Alternatively custody prizes through a trusted adapter or vault whose ledger is authoritative independently of arbitrary collection self-reports.
- Do not represent arbitrary prize contracts as trustlessly verified.
- Gate sponsor/treasury release on successful delivery or a bounded delivery-failure resolution, while recognizing that this mitigates loss but does not make a malicious token truthful.
- Separate receipt from activation so the factory activates only after the external transfer and custody checks return.

Evidence: [source-first finding](/Users/hishamel-husseini/Documents/projects/raffle-fun/audits/2026-10-21-r001/runs/DAYBREAK-TOB/attempt-03/FIRST-PASS.md), [S6 detailed finding](/Users/hishamel-husseini/Documents/projects/raffle-fun/audits/2026-10-21-r001/runs/DAYBREAK-TOB/attempt-03/artifacts/stages/06-secure-workflow/properties/FINDINGS.md).

### DAYBREAK-F-02 — Medium — Prize delivery skips contract-recipient acceptance

**Confidence:** High.

**Affected code and functions:**

- [`redeemWinningTicket`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:304), especially lines 320–337.
- [`releaseSponsorPrize`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:395).
- ERC-721 safe/unsafe semantics in [`IERC721.sol`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/node_modules/@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC721/IERC721.sol:42).

**Lineage:** S3 M-02; S4 contract-winner documentation gap; S5 U-10; source-first `FP-SEC-02`; S6-02.

**Dynamic status:** Confirmed. A contract accepted the safely minted raffle ticket but was intentionally incompatible with the prize. Redemption burned the ticket and transferred the prize without any prize receiver callback.

**Exploit and preconditions:** A contract-valued ticket owner or sponsor recipient can own the relevant claim but cannot accept or operate the prize NFT. Both outbound paths use `transferFrom`, so receiver rejection is never consulted.

**Impact:** A valuable NFT can become irrecoverably held by an incompatible contract even though the transaction reports successful delivery.

**Remediation direction:** Use `safeTransferFrom(address(this), recipient, prizeTokenId)` for winner delivery and sponsor return. Retain checks-effects-interactions and `nonReentrant` so callback rejection restores the ticket, flags, and custody atomically.

### DAYBREAK-F-03 — Low — Clone-destination isolation is incomplete

**Confidence:** High for the source paths; deployed incidence unknown.

**Affected code and functions:**

- [`RaffleFactory.createRaffle` and `_validateCreateParams`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol:97).
- [`Raffle.initialize`, `_update`, `_transferQuote`, `_isProtocolDestination`, and `releaseSponsorPrize`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:176).
- Ordinary CREATE clone deployment in [`Clones.sol`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/node_modules/@openzeppelin/contracts/proxy/Clones.sol:47).

**Lineage:** S4 S4-SEC-02; S5 F-02/REQ-44/REQ-47; source-first `FP-SEC-03`; S6-03.

Two related variants are consolidated:

1. **Future same-factory clone:** a predicted, currently code-less clone address passes initial validation. After deployment and registration, quote release rechecks and becomes blocked, while prize return does not recheck and can move the NFT into the later clone.
2. **Other-factory clone:** `_isProtocolDestination` consults only the local factory registry, so a clone from another factory can receive tickets or other relationships.

**Dynamic status:** The cross-factory variant was reproduced by `test_Evidence_CrossFactoryRaffleDestinationIsAcceptedAndStrandsTicket`, and its desired negative property failed intentionally. The future same-factory variant remains source-established but was not dynamically reproduced; actual factory nonce, recipient state, and transaction ordering remain external leads. S6’s `DST-01` pass covered already registered local sinks and does not refute the future-address path.

**Impact:** Assets or claims can be stranded in a raffle clone outside its accounting. In the future-address variant, the selecting sponsor’s proceeds can become unclaimable while an NFT can be transferred between clones. A configured treasury equal to a future clone address could also make creation at the relevant nonce repeatedly revert.

**Severity adjudication:** S4 and the source-first synthesis rated the future-address issue Low; S5 rated it High; S6 rated the related cross-factory issue Low. The final rating is **Low** because exploitation generally requires deliberate recipient selection, nonce/order coordination or cross-deployment targeting, and no affected deployment was established. The literal invariant violation and potential asset loss are nevertheless retained.

**Remediation direction:**

- Use a shared canonical deployment registry if the no-clone-destination invariant is global.
- Recheck the current destination before prize return as well as quote transfer.
- Reject reserved or predicted factory clone addresses in deployment tooling.
- Provide a narrowly scoped, evented recovery or recipient-rotation mechanism for a destination that later becomes unsafe.
- If isolation is intentionally factory-local, narrow the design and API claim accordingly.

### DAYBREAK-F-04 — Low — Prize callback can create ticket state before canonical publication

**Confidence:** High.

**Affected code and functions:**

- Registry, external prize call, and event ordering in [`RaffleFactory.createRaffle`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol:123).
- Activation in [`Raffle.onERC721Received`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:416).
- [`Raffle.buyEntries`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:209).

**Lineage:** S3 L-01; S4 two-phase-activation recommendation; noted but folded into FP-SEC-01 in the source-first report; separated and reproduced as S6-04.

**Dynamic status:** Confirmed. `test_Evidence_PrizeCanBuyEntriesBeforeCreateRaffleReturns` created a paid entry and ticket from within the sponsor-selected prize transfer, before `RaffleCreated`.

**Exploit and preconditions:** The prize callback changes the clone to `Active` before the outer factory call completes. The factory’s reentrancy guard does not protect the clone’s separate guard slot, so the prize contract can call `buyEntries` during creation.

**Impact:** Sponsor-controlled code can preallocate paid tickets and shape apparent participation or reserve progress before canonical creation publication. The entry remains paid and visible once the transaction lands, limiting severity.

**Remediation direction:** Keep the clone in `AwaitingPrize` during the callback. Let only the factory perform a separate final activation after custody checks, with explicitly documented event ordering.

### DAYBREAK-F-05 — Informational/conditional — Nominal quote accounting depends on official fee-free token behavior

**Confidence:** High for the conditional behavior; applicability to deployment is unverified.

**Affected code and functions:**

- Quote-token constructor validation in [`RaffleFactory.constructor`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol:58).
- Nominal purchase accounting in [`Raffle.buyEntries`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:209).
- Payout helper in [`Raffle._transferQuote`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:560).

**Lineage:** S3 M-01; S5’s dropped REQ-06 candidate; source-first lead L-03; S6-05.

**Dynamic status:** A fee-on-transfer mock confirmed the assumption boundary: buying ten entries recorded 10,000,000 units while custody increased by 9,900,000. This is not evidence that official USDC behaves that way.

**Impact:** A fee-on-transfer, rebasing, no-op, or malicious six-decimal token can make recorded liabilities exceed custody.

**Severity adjudication:** S3 rated the issue Medium conditionally. S5 correctly rejected a requirement for on-chain canonical-address attestation because `DESIGN.md` treats the token as a trusted deployment dependency. S6 classified it Informational/conditional. The final result adopts **Informational/conditional**: the code path is demonstrated, but deployment data identifying the actual quote token is absent.

**Remediation direction:** Pin chain ID, official token address, runtime code, proxy implementation/admin, and expected transfer behavior in deployment automation and post-deployment assertions. If arbitrary quote tokens are supported later, account from observed balance deltas and separately address rebasing and callbacks.

## Specification and documentation divergences

### DAYBREAK-DIV-01 — Low — Sponsor-only early closure of an empty raffle is absent from `DESIGN.md`

**Confidence:** High.

[`Raffle.enableRefunds`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:275) lets the sponsor move an `Active`, zero-entry raffle into `Refunding` before `endTime`; [`IRaffle.sol`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/interfaces/IRaffle.sol:322) documents that behavior. `DESIGN.md` only says refunds open at the deadline.

S5 rated this Medium under REQ-35. The source-first report reduced it to Low, and the final judgment retains **Low as a design-code divergence**, not a hidden access-control vulnerability: the branch requires zero sold entries, so no ticket holder loses a refund. S6’s AUTH-05 pass confirms that the code follows its interface-level sponsor authorization; it does not reconcile the design prose.

Remediation is to remove the early bypass or explicitly disclose sponsor cancellation and early prize return in the design, frontend, and product terms.

### DAYBREAK-OOS-01 — Informational — Frontend current-state rereads are unverifiable

`DESIGN.md` requires discovery data to remain advisory and the frontend to reread current chain state before transaction decisions. The frozen audit target contains no frontend revision. Contract getters and transaction-time checks reduce stale-state consequences but cannot prove frontend pre-decision behavior.

This is not evidence that a deployed frontend violates the requirement. Supply the exact frontend/indexer/keeper repository and revision for review, or explicitly exclude this requirement from the contract target’s compliance claim.

Use when starting an audit, threat model, or architecture review on unfamiliar code, and before any vulnerability-hunting pass.\\\\nallowed-tools: Workflow Task Read Grep Glob\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Audit Context Building\\\\n\\\\nBuild understanding, not verdicts. This runs before anyone hunts for bugs, and feeds that work.\\\\n\\\\n## When to Use\\\\n\\\\nAt the start of an audit, a threat model, or an architecture review, when the code is unfamiliar. Also when\\\\nan earlier pass produced findings nobody could judge, because no one had mapped out how the system fits\\\\ntogether.\\\\n\\\\n## When NOT to Use\\\\n\\\\nDo not name vulnerabilities, suggest fixes, write proofs-of-concept, or rate severity. Those belong to the\\\\nhunting phase, which runs next and with the whole picture in hand. When the code counts on something and\\\\nnothing checks it, record that plainly and move on — whether it matters is decided later.\\\\n\\\\nNot worth the tokens on code you already understand.\\\\n\\\\n## Do not analyze in this context\\\\n\\\\nThe analysis is long, and this context needs to survive to use it. Dispatch it:\\\\n\\\\n- **A codebase, or more than one function** — run `/audit-context-building:audit-context <path>`. It orients,\\\\n  analyzes each function in its own subagent, and writes `audit-context/DOSSIER.md` plus one file per\\\\n  function under `audit-context/functions/`. Only compact records return here.\\\\n- **A single function** — dispatch the `audit-context-building:function-analyzer` agent at it. It writes its\\\\n  prose to disk and returns a record.\\\\n\\\\nThen work from what comes back: the index, the unenforced assumptions, the open questions. Read a function's\\\\nfile when you need its detail.\\\\n\\\\nThe workflow is what enforces this, not this text: a subagent bound to a return schema cannot return prose.\\\\nTreat this section as routing, and route.\\\\n\\\\n## What comes back, and how to read it\\\\n\\\\nEach record lists what must always be true (with the line that shows it), what the function takes on faith\\\\n(with whatever establishes it), which functions it calls and what it needs from each, and anything still\\\\nunclear. The dossier adds the rules that span several functions, who can reach what, and where the\\\\ncomplicated parts cluster.\\\\n\\\\nTwo things matter more than the rest:\\\\n\\\\n- **Assumptions marked `nothing found`.** The code counts on something being true and nothing anywhere makes\\\\n  it true. This is the most useful thing to hand the hunting phase.\\\\n- **The open questions.** An honest list of what is still unclear beats a confident answer that turns out to\\\\n  be wrong. Carry them forward instead of closing them out.\\\\n\\\\nWhere two records disagree, both are quoted rather than quietly reconciled. That is a fact about the code,\\\\nnot a flaw in the analysis.\\\\n\\\\n## The format\\\\n\\\\n[ANALYSIS_FORMAT.md](resources/ANALYSIS_FORMAT.md) defines it, and\\\\n[FUNCTION_MICRO_ANALYSIS_EXAMPLE.md](resources/FUNCTION_MICRO_ANALYSIS_EXAMPLE.md) works through examples in\\\\nC and Solidity. Read them when extending this plugin or deciding whether a record can be trusted.\\\\n\\\\nThe format is the same whatever the target. What changes is what fills each slot, and what counts as a call\\\\nyou cannot see inside. [DOMAIN_NOTES.md](resources/DOMAIN_NOTES.md) maps that across smart contracts, C and\\\\nC++, decompiled firmware, and web services — read it when the target is not plain source code.\\\\n\\\\n**The rule that matters most: follow the calls.** Whether a function is correct usually depends on something\\\\nanother function does, and you cannot see that from the caller alone. A limit looks enforced because the\\\\nvalue came back from a function whose name suggests it was checked. So read the function being called, follow\\\\nevery path through it rather than only the one that succeeds, and say what makes each assumption true. When\\\\nnothing does, use those words: `nothing found`. Every claim cites a line, or becomes an open question.\\\\nFILE /Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/upstreams/trailofbits/plugins/entry-point-analyzer/skills/entry-point-analyzer/SKILL.md\\\\n---\\\\nname: entry-point-analyzer\\\\ndescription: Analyzes smart contract codebases to identify state-changing entry points for security auditing. Detects externally callable functions that modify state, categorizes them by access level (public, admin, role-restricted, contract-only), and generates structured audit reports. Excludes view/pure/read-only functions. Use when auditing smart contracts (Solidity, Vyper, Solana/Rust, Move, TON, CosmWasm) or when asked to find entry points, audit flows, external functions, access control patterns, or privileged operations.\\\\nallowed-tools: Read Grep Glob Bash\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Entry Point Analyzer\\\\n\\\\nSystematically identify all **state-changing** entry points in a smart contract codebase to guide security audits.\\\\n\\\\n## When to Use\\\\n\\\\nUse this skill when:\\\\n- Starting a smart contract security audit to map the attack surface\\\\n- Asked to find entry points, external functions, or audit flows\\\\n- Analyzing access control patterns across a codebase\\\\n- Identifying privileged operations and role-restricted functions\\\\n- Building an understanding of which functions can modify contract state\\\\n\\\\n## When NOT to Use\\\\n\\\\nDo NOT use this skill for:\\\\n- Vulnerability detection (use audit-context-building or domain-specific-audits)\\\\n- Writing exploit POCs (use solidity-poc-builder)\\\\n- Code quality or gas optimization analysis\\\\n- Non-smart-contract codebases\\\\n- Analyzing read-only functions (this skill excludes them)\\\\n\\\\n## Scope: State-Changing Functions Only\\\\n\\\\nThis skill focuses exclusively on functions that can modify state. **Excluded:**\\\\n\\\\n| Language | Excluded Patterns |\\\\n|----------|-------------------|\\\\n| Solidity | `view`, `pure` functions |\\\\n| Vyper | `@view`, `@pure` functions |\\\\n| Solana | Functions without `mut` account references |\\\\n| Move | Non-entry `public fun` (module-callable only) |\\\\n| TON | `get` methods (FunC), read-only receivers (Tact) |\\\\n| CosmWasm | `query` entry point and its handlers |\\\\n\\\\n**Why exclude read-only functions?** They cannot directly cause loss of funds or state corruption. While they may leak information, the primary audit focus is on functions that can change state.\\\\n\\\\n## Workflow\\\\n\\\\n1. **Detect Language** - Identify contract language(s) from file extensions and syntax\\\\n2. **Use Tooling (if available)** - For Solidity, check if Slither is available and use it\\\\n3. **Locate Contracts** - Find all contract/module files (apply directory filter if specified)\\\\n4. **Extract Entry Points** - Parse each file for externally callable, state-changing functions\\\\n5. **Classify Access** - Categorize each function by access level\\\\n6. **Generate Report** - Output structured markdown report\\\\n\\\\n## Slither Integration (Solidity)\\\\n\\\\nFor Solidity codebases, Slither can automatically extract entry points. Before manual analysis:\\\\n\\\\n### 1. Check if Slither is Available\\\\n\\\\n```bash\\\\nwhich slither\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n### 2. If Slither is Detected, Run Entry Points Printer\\\\n\\\\n```bash\\\\nslither . --print entry-points\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nThis outputs a table of all state-changing entry points with:\\\\n- Contract name\\\\n- Function name\\\\n- Visibility\\\\n- Modifiers applied\\\\n\\\\n### 3. Use Slither Output as Foundation\\\\n\\\\n- Parse the Slither output table to populate your analysis\\\\n- Cross-reference with manual inspection for access control classification\\\\n- Slither may miss some patterns (callbacks, dynamic access control)—supplement with manual review\\\\n- If Slither fails (compilation errors, unsupported features), fall back to manual analysis\\\\n\\\\n### 4. When Slither is NOT Available\\\\n\\\\nIf `which slither` returns nothing, proceed with manual analysis using the language-specific reference files.\\\\n\\\\n## Language Detection\\\\n\\\\n| Extension | Language | Reference |\\\\n|-----------|----------|-----------|\\\\n| `.sol` | Solidity | [{baseDir}/references/solidity.md]({baseDir}/references/solidity.md) |\\\\n| `.vy` | Vyper | [{baseDir}/references/vyper.md]({baseDir}/references/vyper.md) |\\\\n| `.rs` + `Cargo.toml` with `solana-program` | Solana (Rust) | [{baseDir}/references/solana.md]({baseDir}/references/solana.md) |\\\\n| `.move` + `Move.toml` with `edition` | [{baseDir}/references/move-sui.md]({baseDir}/references/move-sui.md) |\\\\n| `.move` + `Move.toml` with `Aptos` | [{baseDir}/references/move-aptos.md]({baseDir}/references/move-aptos.md) |\\\\n| `.fc`, `.func`, `.tact` | TON (FunC/Tact) | [{baseDir}/references/ton.md]({baseDir}/references/ton.md) |\\\\n| `.rs` + `Cargo.toml` with `cosmwasm-std` | CosmWasm | [{baseDir}/references/cosmwasm.md]({baseDir}/references/cosmwasm.md) |\\\\n\\\\nLoad the appropriate reference file(s) based on detected language before analysis.\\\\n\\\\n## Access Classification\\\\n\\\\nClassify each state-changing entry point into one of these categories:\\\\n\\\\n### 1. Public (Unrestricted)\\\\nFunctions callable by anyone without restrictions.\\\\n\\\\n### 2. Role-Restricted\\\\nFunctions limited to specific roles. Common patterns to detect:\\\\n- Explicit role names: `admin`, `owner`, `governance`, `guardian`, `operator`, `manager`, `minter`, `pauser`, `keeper`, `relayer`, `lender`, `borrower`\\\\n- Role-checking patterns: `onlyRole`, `hasRole`, `require(msg.sender == X)`, `assert_owner`, `#[access_control]`\\\\n- When role is ambiguous, flag as **\\\\\\\"Restricted (review required)\\\\\\\"** with the restriction pattern noted\\\\n\\\\n### 3. Contract-Only (Internal Integration Points)\\\\nFunctions callable only by other contracts, not by EOAs. Indicators:\\\\n- Callbacks: `onERC721Received`, `uniswapV3SwapCallback`, `flashLoanCallback`\\\\n- Interface implementations with contract-caller checks\\\\n- Functions that revert if `tx.origin == msg.sender`\\\\n- Cross-contract hooks\\\\n\\\\n## Output Format\\\\n\\\\nGenerate a markdown report with this structure:\\\\n\\\\n```markdown\\\\n# Entry Point Analysis: [Project Name]\\\\n\\\\n**Analyzed**: [timestamp]\\\\n**Scope**: [directories analyzed or \\\\\\\"full codebase\\\\\\\"]\\\\n**Languages**: [detected languages]\\\\n**Focus**: State-changing functions only (view/pure excluded)\\\\n\\\\n## Summary\\\\n\\\\n| Category | Count |\\\\n|----------|-------|\\\\n| Public (Unrestricted) | X |\\\\n| Role-Restricted | X |\\\\n| Restricted (Review Required) | X |\\\\n| Contract-Only | X |\\\\n| **Total** | **X** |\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Public Entry Points (Unrestricted)\\\\n\\\\nState-changing functions callable by anyone—prioritize for attack surface The documentation says what the system does; the code\\\\ndecides what it actually does. Every gap between them is either a bug or a documentation fix, and which one it\\\\nis is the finding.\\\\n\\\\n## When to Use\\\\n\\\\nYou have both documentation describing intended behavior and the code that should implement it. A whitepaper\\\\nagainst a protocol, a design note against a service, a README's stated guarantees against the functions behind\\\\nthem.\\\\n\\\\nMost useful when the document is authoritative — something a client wrote, published, or is audited against —\\\\nbecause then a divergence is a defect rather than stale prose.\\\\n\\\\n## When NOT to Use\\\\n\\\\nNot for code with no documentation of intended behavior. There is nothing to check against, and a requirement\\\\ninferred from the code is checked against itself. Build the system model first with `audit-context-building`.\\\\n\\\\nNot for finding bugs in general. This finds one class: where the code and the document disagree. A bug both\\\\nartifacts are silent about is out of scope, and a bug the document endorses is a finding against the document.\\\\n\\\\nNot for writing or improving documentation, though it produces the list of what needs fixing.\\\\n\\\\n## Do not check requirements in this context\\\\n\\\\nRun `/spec-to-code-compliance:spec-compliance <path>`. The slash command takes a path; to name the\\\\nspecification directly or widen the fan-out, ask for the run with those values — \\\\\\\"run spec-compliance on\\\\n./contracts against SPEC.md, checking 20 requirements\\\\\\\" — and they reach the script as `{path, spec, limit}`.\\\\nTyping the object literally after the slash command does not work; it arrives as a string and becomes the path.\\\\n\\\\nIt finds the documents, splits them into individually checkable requirements, gives each requirement its own\\\\nagent to hunt the code with, has independent agents try to refute every divergence before it is reported, and\\\\nwrites `spec-compliance/REPORT.md` plus one file per requirement under `spec-compliance/requirements/`. Only\\\\ncompact records come back here.\\\\n\\\\nFor a single requirement, dispatch the `spec-to-code-compliance:spec-compliance-checker` agent at it.\\\\n\\\\nThis is not a preference about where output lands. The check does not fit in one context window if it is done\\\\nhonestly: judging one requirement means reading the enforcement, its callees, and its callers, and doing that\\\\nfor thirty requirements means holding thirty call chains at once. Attempted inline, the first few get a real\\\\ncheck and the rest get a plausible one — and the transcript looks the same either way, because a verdict resting\\\\non a promising function name reads exactly like one resting on having read the function. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Finish monitoring the existing isolated scan; resume its diagnosed failed jobs.

No new scan, replacement reviewer, model substitution or native result rewriting.
Only the two previously diagnosed model_process_error rows are eligible here.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import re
import subprocess
import time
import urllib.request

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
OUT = ROOT / "provider-lanes/claude/runs/CLAUDE-OPENKRITT-MOD/attempt-01/native-resume-supervisor"
HOST = "unix:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.lima/raffle-claude-openkritt/sock/docker.sock"
URL = "http://127.0.0.1:3002/api/scans/1"


def now():
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()


def sql(query):
    # Normal use of the container's own database credentials. No credential
    # values leave the container or appear in this process's argv/output.
    command = ["docker", "--host", HOST, "exec", "open-kritt-db", "sh", "-c",
               'PGPASSWORD="$POSTGRES_PASSWORD" exec psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB" -At -c "$1"',
               "audit-readonly-sql", query]
    return subprocess.check_output(command, text=True)


def record(name, data):
    (OUT / name).write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2) + "\n")


def preserve_model_error_outputs(failed):
    """Copy the original failed-process diagnostics out of the isolated VM."""
    destination = OUT / "preserved-model-error-outputs"
    destination.mkdir()
    manifest = {}
    for row in failed:
        match = re.search(r"model output:\s*(/data/model-error-outputs/[^;\s]+)", row.get("error", ""))
        assert match, ("Missing saved model-output path", row)
        source = match.group(1)
        name = Path(source).name
        subprocess.run(["docker", "--host", HOST, "cp",
                        f"open-kritt-engine:{source}", str(destination / name)], check=True)
        for path in sorted((destination / name).rglob("*")):
            if path.is_file():
                manifest[path.relative_to(OUT).as_posix()] = {
                    "bytes": path.stat().st_size,
                    "sha256": hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
                }
    record("preserved-model-error-outputs-manifest.json", {
        "captured_at": now(),
        "files": manifest,
        "original_failed_metadata_ids": [row["id"] for row in failed],
    })


OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=False)
record("launch.json", {"started_at": now(), "scan_url": URL, "docker_host": HOST,
                       "existing_scan_only": True, "eligible_failed_ids": [21, 22],
                       "outer_deadline": None, "automatic_safety_refusal_retry": False})
resumed = False
while True:
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(URL, timeout=20) as response:
            scan = json.load(response)
        assert str(scan["id"]) == "1" and scan["repoFull"] == "raffle-fun-r001-clean"
        assert scan["model"] == "claude-opus-5-5" and scan["thinkingEffort"] == "max"
        assert scan["harness"] == "claude-code"
        summary = scan.get("statusSummary", {})
        safe = {"observed_at": now(), "status": scan["status"],
                "progress": scan.get("progress"), "progressLabel": scan.get("progressLabel"),
                "counts": {key: summary.get(key) for key in ["completedAttempts", "runningAttempts", "failedAttempts", "currentFailedAttempts", "activeJobCount", "canResume", "postCompletedAttempts", "postRunningAttempts"]}}
        with (OUT / "observations.jsonl").open("a") as stream:
            stream.write(json.dumps(safe) + "\n")
        if scan["status"] == "completed" and summary.get("activeJobCount") == 0:
            record("native-terminal.json", safe)
            break
        if scan["status"] in ["failed", "paused", "stopped"] and summary.get("activeJobCount") == 0 and not resumed:
            # Refuse to operate on an unexpectedly reused database.
            assert sql("SELECT count(*)::text FROM workflows.scans;").strip() == "1"
            failed = [json.loads(line) for line in sql("SELECT row_to_json(q) FROM (SELECT id::text, status, error FROM workflows.step_metadata WHERE scan_id=1 AND status='failed' ORDER BY id) q;").splitlines()]
            assert {int(row["id"]) for row in failed} == {21, 22}, "Unexpected failed metadata lineage"
            assert all("model_process_error" in str(row.get("error", "")) for row in failed), "Undiagnosed failure; no automatic transition"
            record("diagnosed-failures-before-resume.json", failed)
            preserve_model_error_outputs(failed)
            dump = OUT / "before-native-resume.sql"
            with dump.open("xb") as destination:
                subprocess.run(["docker", "--host", HOST, "exec", "open-kritt-db", "sh", "-c",
                                'PGPASSWORD="$POSTGRES_PASSWORD" exec pg_dump -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB" --schema=workflows --no-owner --no-privileges'],
                               stdout=destination, check=True)
            record("pre-resume-seal.json", {"captured_at": now(), "path": dump.name,
                                           "sha256": hashlib.sha256(dump.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
                                           "existing_results_rewritten": False})
            request = urllib.request.Request(URL, data=b'{"status":"pending"}',
                                             headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="PATCH")
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=20) as response:
                result = json.load(response)
            resumed = True
            record("native-resume-receipt.json", {"resumed_at": now(), "method": "PATCH", "url": URL,
                                                  "body": {"status": "pending"}, "returned_scan_id": result.get("id"),
                                                  "returned_status": result.get("status"),
                                                  "preserved_pre_resume_dump": dump.name,
                                                  "direct_database_mutation": False, "new_scan_created": False})
        elif scan["status"] in ["failed", "paused", "stopped"] and summary.get("activeJobCount") == 0:
            record("needs-operational-diagnosis.json", safe)
    except Exception as error:
        # Preserve diagnostics; an operational error does not terminate the lane.
        with (OUT / "operational-errors.jsonl").open("a") as stream:
            stream.write(json.dumps({"observed_at": now(), "error": str(error)}) + "\n")
    time.sleep(20)

### DAYBREAK-F-01 — Critical — An untrusted prize can fake escrow and delivery while buyer-funded proceeds are released

**Confidence:** High.

**Affected code and functions:**

- [`RaffleFactory.createRaffle`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol:97), including prize transfer/postconditions at lines 127–147.

- [`Raffle.onERC721Received`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:416).
- Prize delivery, settlement, and releases in [`Raffle.sol`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:304).
- Conflicting trust statement in [`IRaffle.sol`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/interfaces/IRaffle.sol:12).

**Lineage:** S3 H-01 and L-01; S4 S4-SEC-01; S5 F-01 covering REQ-14, REQ-48, and REQ-53; source-first `FP-SEC-01`; S6-01.

**Dynamic status:** Confirmed. `test_Evidence_MaliciousPrizeCanFakeEscrowAndDelivery` completed creation, purchase, draw, settlement, sponsor and treasury release, and purported delivery. The buyer became the prize’s reported owner while the mock’s separate actual owner remained the malicious sponsor. The desired negative property failed intentionally.

**Exploit and preconditions:** A malicious sponsor selects a contract that reports ERC-721 support, invokes the expected receiver callback without transferring a genuine asset, and lies through `ownerOf`. Entrants then pay real quote tokens. With a trivially met reserve, the raffle reaches `NftWon`; 95% can be released to the sponsor recipient and 5% to treasury before trustworthy prize delivery exists. The token may later revert forever or fabricate successful delivery.

**Impact:** Direct, source-uncapped buyer loss and fraudulent raffle publication. There is no `NftWon` transition to refunds after proceeds have been released.

**Severity adjudication:** S3, S4, and S6 rated the issue High; S5 and the sealed source-first synthesis rated it Critical. The final rating is **Critical** because S6 confirmed the complete buyer-loss and proceeds-release sequence, while source imposes no pot cap. The malicious-sponsor and entrant-participation preconditions are retained rather than hidden.

**Remediation direction:**

- Enforce a deployment-specific allowlist or attested immutable collection registry, including upgrade/admin provenance.
- Alternatively custody prizes through a trusted adapter or vault whose ledger is authoritative independently of arbitrary collection self-reports.
- Do not represent arbitrary prize contracts as trustlessly verified.
- Gate sponsor/treasury release on successful delivery or a bounded delivery-failure resolution, while recognizing that this mitigates loss but does not make a malicious token truthful.
- Separate receipt from activation so the factory activates only after the external transfer and custody checks return.

Evidence: [source-first finding](/Users/hishamel-husseini/Documents/projects/raffle-fun/audits/2026-10-21-r001/runs/DAYBREAK-TOB/attempt-03/FIRST-PASS.md), [S6 detailed finding](/Users/hishamel-husseini/Documents/projects/raffle-fun/audits/2026-10-21-r001/runs/DAYBREAK-TOB/attempt-03/artifacts/stages/06-secure-workflow/properties/FINDINGS.md).

### DAYBREAK-F-02 — Medium — Prize delivery skips contract-recipient acceptance

**Confidence:** High.

**Affected code and functions:**

- [`redeemWinningTicket`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:304), especially lines 320–337.
- [`releaseSponsorPrize`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:395).
- ERC-721 safe/unsafe semantics in [`IERC721.sol`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/node_modules/@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC721/IERC721.sol:42).

**Lineage:** S3 M-02; S4 contract-winner documentation gap; S5 U-10; source-first `FP-SEC-02`; S6-02.

**Dynamic status:** Confirmed. A contract accepted the safely minted raffle ticket but was intentionally incompatible with the prize. Redemption burned the ticket and transferred the prize without any prize receiver callback.

**Exploit and preconditions:** A contract-valued ticket owner or sponsor recipient can own the relevant claim but cannot accept or operate the prize NFT. Both outbound paths use `transferFrom`, so receiver rejection is never consulted.

**Impact:** A valuable NFT can become irrecoverably held by an incompatible contract even though the transaction reports successful delivery.

**Remediation direction:** Use `safeTransferFrom(address(this), recipient, prizeTokenId)` for winner delivery and sponsor return. Retain checks-effects-interactions and `nonReentrant` so callback rejection restores the ticket, flags, and custody atomically.

**Affected code and functions:**

- [`RaffleFactory.createRaffle` and `_validateCreateParams`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol:97).
- [`Raffle.initialize`, `_update`, `_transferQuote`, `_isProtocolDestination`, and `releaseSponsorPrize`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:176).
- Ordinary CREATE clone deployment in [`Clones.sol`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/node_modules/@openzeppelin/contracts/proxy/Clones.sol:47).

**Lineage:** S4 S4-SEC-02; S5 F-02/REQ-44/REQ-47; source-first `FP-SEC-03`; S6-03.

Two related variants are consolidated:

1. **Future same-factory clone:** a predicted, currently code-less clone address passes initial validation. After deployment and registration, quote release rechecks and becomes blocked, while prize return does not recheck and can move the NFT into the later clone.
2. **Other-factory clone:** `_isProtocolDestination` consults only the local factory registry, so a clone from another factory can receive tickets or other relationships.

**Dynamic status:** The cross-factory variant was reproduced by `test_Evidence_CrossFactoryRaffleDestinationIsAcceptedAndStrandsTicket`, and its desired negative property failed intentionally. The future same-factory variant remains source-established but was not dynamically reproduced; actual factory nonce, recipient state, and transaction ordering remain external leads. S6’s `DST-01` pass covered already registered local sinks and does not refute the future-address path.

**Impact:** Assets or claims can be stranded in a raffle clone outside its accounting. In the future-address variant, the selecting sponsor’s proceeds can become unclaimable while an NFT can be transferred between clones. A configured treasury equal to a future clone address could also make creation at the relevant nonce repeatedly revert.

**Severity adjudication:** S4 and the source-first synthesis rated the future-address issue Low; S5 rated it High; S6 rated the related cross-factory issue Low. The final rating is **Low** because exploitation generally requires deliberate recipient selection, nonce/order coordination or cross-deployment targeting, and no affected deployment was established. The literal invariant violation and potential asset loss are nevertheless retained.

**Remediation direction:**

- Use a shared canonical deployment registry if the no-clone-destination invariant is global.
- Recheck the current destination before prize return as well as quote transfer.
- Reject reserved or predicted factory clone addresses in deployment tooling.
- Provide a narrowly scoped, evented recovery or recipient-rotation mechanism for a destination that later becomes unsafe.
- If isolation is intentionally factory-local, narrow the design and API claim accordingly.

### DAYBREAK-F-04 — Low — Prize callback can create ticket state before canonical publication

**Confidence:** High.

**Affected code and functions:**

- Registry, external prize call, and event ordering in [`RaffleFactory.createRaffle`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol:123).
- Activation in [`Raffle.onERC721Received`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:416).
- [`Raffle.buyEntries`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:209).

**Lineage:** S3 L-01; S4 two-phase-activation recommendation; noted but folded into FP-SEC-01 in the source-first report; separated and reproduced as S6-04.

**Dynamic status:** Confirmed. `test_Evidence_PrizeCanBuyEntriesBeforeCreateRaffleReturns` created a paid entry and ticket from within the sponsor-selected prize transfer, before `RaffleCreated`.

**Exploit and preconditions:** The prize callback changes the clone to `Active` before the outer factory call completes. The factory’s reentrancy guard does not protect the clone’s separate guard slot, so the prize contract can call `buyEntries` during creation.

**Impact:** Sponsor-controlled code can preallocate paid tickets and shape apparent participation or reserve progress before canonical creation publication. The entry remains paid and visible once the transaction lands, limiting severity.

**Remediation direction:** Keep the clone in `AwaitingPrize` during the callback. Let only the factory perform a separate final activation after custody checks, with explicitly documented event ordering.

S5 rated this Medium under REQ-35. The source-first report reduced it to Low, and the final judgment retains **Low as a design-code divergence**, not a hidden access-control vulnerability: the branch requires zero sold entries, so no ticket holder loses a refund. S6’s AUTH-05 pass confirms that the code follows its interface-level sponsor authorization; it does not reconcile the design prose.

Remediation is to remove the early bypass or explicitly disclose sponsor cancellation and early prize return in the design, frontend, and product terms.

### DAYBREAK-OOS-01 — Informational — Frontend current-state rereads are unverifiable

`DESIGN.md` requires discovery data to remain advisory and the frontend to reread current chain state before transaction decisions. The frozen audit target contains no frontend revision. Contract getters and transaction-time checks reduce stale-state consequences but cannot prove frontend pre-decision behavior.

This is not evidence that a deployed frontend violates the requirement. Supply the exact frontend/indexer/keeper repository and revision for review, or explicitly exclude this requirement from the contract target’s compliance claim.

### Other documentation gaps

S5’s 11 reverse-sweep behaviors remain documented without inflating the finding count:

| ID | Omitted behavior |
|---|---|
| U-01 | Positive reserve and 30-day maximum sale duration |
| U-02 | Depositor and immutable `sponsorRecipient` may differ |
| U-03 | Ticket destinations exclude several protocol addresses, not only clones |
| U-04 | Draw requests are caller-funded native-token operations with one word, 300,000 callback gas, 30 confirmations, and an atomic excess refund |
| U-05 | Authenticated but unusable callbacks emit and return rather than reverting |
| U-06 | Winning entry is `(randomWord % totalEntries) + 1` |
| U-07 | Zero-entry sponsor cancellation before deadline |
| U-08 | Refund calls accept at most 100 ticket IDs |
| U-09 | Releases are permissionless pushes to fixed recipients |
| U-10 | Outbound prize delivery skips receiver acceptance |
| U-11 | Unsolicited NFTs sent with unsafe `transferFrom` can be stranded without rescue |

Additional documentation defects are the direct `DESIGN.md`/`IRaffle.sol` prize-trust contradiction, ambiguous use of “sponsor,” absence of a named frontend revision, creation-event ordering, ignored-callback reason opacity, and missing deployment-attestation and migration/runoff procedures.

### S5 candidates correctly dropped after refutation

- REQ-06: canonical USDC identity is a deployment premise, not an on-chain identity-attestation requirement.

No native sample diff is approved for production:

- Gating quote claims on `prizeClaimed` alone can convert a malicious-prize failure into indefinite locked liabilities and must cover sponsor and protocol claims plus an exact refund/fallback design.

- A maximum reserve constant is not present in the frozen source and cannot be invented without product/economic specification.
- Early cancellation after paid entries changes purchaser rights and requires a full liability transition, not the proposed local branch edit.
- `safeTransferFrom` receiver acceptance does not prove later bearer capability, and silently redirecting the configured sponsor recipient changes ownership policy.
- Disallowing draws below reserve removes the specified CashWon path rather than fixing a demonstrated defect.
- The separately registered broken Pashov Option C fallback remains `AQ-008`: it omits unsettled NftWon liability and can underflow refund subtraction. It is not applied or recommended as validated.

**Lineage:** S3 H-01 and L-01; S4 S4-SEC-01; S5 F-01 covering REQ-14, REQ-48, and REQ-53; source-first `FP-SEC-01`; S6-01.

**Dynamic status:** Confirmed. `test_Evidence_MaliciousPrizeCanFakeEscrowAndDelivery` completed creation, purchase, draw, settlement, sponsor and treasury release, and purported delivery. The buyer became the prize’s reported owner while the mock’s separate actual owner remained the malicious sponsor. The desired negative property failed intentionally.

**Exploit and preconditions:** A malicious sponsor selects a contract that reports ERC-721 support, invokes the expected receiver callback without transferring a genuine asset, and lies through `ownerOf`. Entrants then pay real quote tokens. With a trivially met reserve, the raffle reaches `NftWon`; 95% can be released to the sponsor recipient and 5% to treasury before trustworthy prize delivery exists. The token may later revert forever or fabricate successful delivery.

**Impact:** Direct, source-uncapped buyer loss and fraudulent raffle publication. There is no `NftWon` transition to refunds after proceeds have been released.

**Severity adjudication:** S3, S4, and S6 rated the issue High; S5 and the sealed source-first synthesis rated it Critical. The final rating is **Critical** because S6 confirmed the complete buyer-loss and proceeds-release sequence, while source imposes no pot cap. The malicious-sponsor and entrant-participation preconditions are retained rather than hidden.

**Remediation direction:**

- Enforce a deployment-specific allowlist or attested immutable collection registry, including upgrade/admin provenance.
- Alternatively custody prizes through a trusted adapter or vault whose ledger is authoritative independently of arbitrary collection self-reports.
- Do not represent arbitrary prize contracts as trustlessly verified.
- Gate sponsor/treasury release on successful delivery or a bounded delivery-failure resolution, while recognizing that this mitigates loss but does not make a malicious token truthful.
- Separate receipt from activation so the factory activates only after the external transfer and custody checks return.

Evidence: [source-first finding](/Users/hishamel-husseini/Documents/projects/raffle-fun/audits/2026-10-21-r001/runs/DAYBREAK-TOB/attempt-03/FIRST-PASS.md), [S6 detailed finding](/Users/hishamel-husseini/Documents/projects/raffle-fun/audits/2026-10-21-r001/runs/DAYBREAK-TOB/attempt-03/artifacts/stages/06-secure-workflow/properties/FINDINGS.md).

### DAYBREAK-F-02 — Medium — Prize delivery skips contract-recipient acceptance

**Confidence:** High.

**Affected code and functions:**

- [`redeemWinningTicket`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:304), especially lines 320–337.
- [`releaseSponsorPrize`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:395).
- ERC-721 safe/unsafe semantics in [`IERC721.sol`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/node_modules/@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC721/IERC721.sol:42).

**Lineage:** S3 M-02; S4 contract-winner documentation gap; S5 U-10; source-first `FP-SEC-02`; S6-02.

**Dynamic status:** Confirmed. A contract accepted the safely minted raffle ticket but was intentionally incompatible with the prize. Redemption burned the ticket and transferred the prize without any prize receiver callback.

**Exploit and preconditions:** A contract-valued ticket owner or sponsor recipient can own the relevant claim but cannot accept or operate the prize NFT. Both outbound paths use `transferFrom`, so receiver rejection is never consulted.

**Impact:** A valuable NFT can become irrecoverably held by an incompatible contract even though the transaction reports successful delivery.

**Remediation direction:** Use `safeTransferFrom(address(this), recipient, prizeTokenId)` for winner delivery and sponsor return. Retain checks-effects-interactions and `nonReentrant` so callback rejection restores the ticket, flags, and custody atomically.

### DAYBREAK-F-03 — Low — Clone-destination isolation is incomplete

**Confidence:** High for the source paths; deployed incidence unknown.

**Affected code and functions:**

- [`RaffleFactory.createRaffle` and `_validateCreateParams`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol:97).
- [`Raffle.initialize`, `_update`, `_transferQuote`, `_isProtocolDestination`, and `releaseSponsorPrize`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:176).
- Ordinary CREATE clone deployment in [`Clones.sol`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/node_modules/@openzeppelin/contracts/proxy/Clones.sol:47).

**Lineage:** S4 S4-SEC-02; S5 F-02/REQ-44/REQ-47; source-first `FP-SEC-03`; S6-03.

Two related variants are consolidated:

1. **Future same-factory clone:** a predicted, currently code-less clone address passes initial validation. After deployment and registration, quote release rechecks and becomes blocked, while prize return does not recheck and can move the NFT into the later clone.
2. **Other-factory clone:** `_isProtocolDestination` consults only the local factory registry, so a clone from another factory can receive tickets or other relationships.

**Dynamic status:** The cross-factory variant was reproduced by `test_Evidence_CrossFactoryRaffleDestinationIsAcceptedAndStrandsTicket`, and its desired negative property failed intentionally. The future same-factory variant remains source-established but was not dynamically reproduced; actual factory nonce, recipient state, and transaction ordering remain external leads. S6’s `DST-01` pass covered already registered local sinks and does not refute the future-address path.

**Impact:** Assets or claims can be stranded in a raffle clone outside its accounting. In the future-address variant, the selecting sponsor’s proceeds can become unclaimable while an NFT can be transferred between clones. A configured treasury equal to a future clone address could also make creation at the relevant nonce repeatedly revert.

**Severity adjudication:** S4 and the source-first synthesis rated the future-address issue Low; S5 rated it High; S6 rated the related cross-factory issue Low. The final rating is **Low** because exploitation generally requires deliberate recipient selection, nonce/order coordination or cross-deployment targeting, and no affected deployment was established. The literal invariant violation and potential asset loss are nevertheless retained.

**Remediation direction:**

- Use a shared canonical deployment registry if the no-clone-destination invariant is global.
- Recheck the current destination before prize return as well as quote transfer.
- Reject reserved or predicted factory clone addresses in deployment tooling.
- Provide a narrowly scoped, evented recovery or recipient-rotation mechanism for a destination that later becomes unsafe.
- If isolation is intentionally factory-local, narrow the design and API claim accordingly.

### DAYBREAK-F-04 — Low — Prize callback can create ticket state before canonical publication

**Confidence:** High.

**Affected code and functions:**

- Registry, external prize call, and event ordering in [`RaffleFactory.createRaffle`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol:123).
- Activation in [`Raffle.onERC721Received`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:416).
- [`Raffle.buyEntries`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:209).

**Lineage:** S3 L-01; S4 two-phase-activation recommendation; noted but folded into FP-SEC-01 in the source-first report; separated and reproduced as S6-04.

**Dynamic status:** Confirmed. `test_Evidence_PrizeCanBuyEntriesBeforeCreateRaffleReturns` created a paid entry and ticket from within the sponsor-selected prize transfer, before `RaffleCreated`.

**Exploit and preconditions:** The prize callback changes the clone to `Active` before the outer factory call completes. The factory’s reentrancy guard does not protect the clone’s separate guard slot, so the prize contract can call `buyEntries` during creation.

**Impact:** Sponsor-controlled code can preallocate paid tickets and shape apparent participation or reserve progress before canonical creation publication. The entry remains paid and visible once the transaction lands, limiting severity.

**Remediation direction:** Keep the clone in `AwaitingPrize` during the callback. Let only the factory perform a separate final activation after custody checks, with explicitly documented event ordering.

## Specification and documentation divergences

### DAYBREAK-DIV-01 — Low — Sponsor-only early closure of an empty raffle is absent from `DESIGN.md`

**Confidence:** High.

[`Raffle.enableRefunds`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:275) lets the sponsor move an `Active`, zero-entry raffle into `Refunding` before `endTime`; [`IRaffle.sol`](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/cells/DAYBREAK-TOB-continuation/target/packages/contracts/src/interfaces/IRaffle.sol:322) documents that behavior. `DESIGN.md` only says refunds open at the deadline.

S5 rated this Medium under REQ-35. The source-first report reduced it to Low, and the final judgment retains **Low as a design-code divergence**, not a hidden access-control vulnerability: the branch requires zero sold entries, so no ticket holder loses a refund. S6’s AUTH-05 pass confirms that the code follows its interface-level sponsor authorization; it does not reconcile the design prose.

Remediation is to remove the early bypass or explicitly disclose sponsor cancellation and early prize return in the design, frontend, and product terms.

### DAYBREAK-OOS-01 — Informational — Frontend current-state rereads are unverifiable

`DESIGN.md` requires discovery data to remain advisory and the frontend to reread current chain state before transaction decisions. The frozen audit target contains no frontend revision. Contract getters and transaction-time checks reduce stale-state consequences but cannot prove frontend pre-decision behavior.

This is not evidence that a deployed frontend violates the requirement. Supply the exact frontend/indexer/keeper repository and revision for review, or explicitly exclude this requirement from the contract target’s compliance claim.

### Other documentation gaps

S5’s 11 reverse-sweep behaviors remain documented without inflating the finding count:

| ID | Omitted behavior |
|---|---|
| U-01 | Positive reserve and 30-day maximum sale duration |
| U-02 | Depositor and immutable `sponsorRecipient` may differ |

| U-04 | Draw requests are caller-funded native-token operations with one word, 300,000 callback gas, 30 confirmations, and an atomic excess refund |
| U-05 | Authenticated but unusable callbacks emit and return rather than reverting |
| U-06 | Winning entry is `(randomWord % totalEntries) + 1` |
| U-07 | Zero-entry sponsor cancellation before deadline |
| U-08 | Refund calls accept at most 100 ticket IDs |
| U-09 | Releases are permissionless pushes to fixed recipients |
| U-10 | Outbound prize delivery skips receiver acceptance |
| U-11 | Unsolicited NFTs sent with unsafe `transferFrom` can be stranded without rescue |

Additional documentation defects are the direct `DESIGN.md`/`IRaffle.sol` prize-trust contradiction, ambiguous use of “sponsor,” absence of a named frontend revision, creation-event ordering, ignored-callback reason opacity, and missing deployment-attestation and migration/runoff procedures.

# raffle.fun audit r001

**Status: INCOMPLETE — current evidence draft.** Required native continuations and provider qualification remain unfinished. This report is not a release approval or a claim that all requested workflows completed. The parent coordinator will update the final status, matrix and integrity record before delivery.

Frozen commit: `9238b6ce8eb7f768c0dcd0cfcef26e1427a03155`. Draft assembled 2026-10-21T18:10:19.029516+00:00; provider-route corrections refreshed 2026-10-21T21:34:34.244518+00:00. The workflow table is an interim snapshot pending the active continuations. No production remediation, deployment or live transaction was performed.

## Assessment

The review identifies two principal source-level root causes. The more consequential is conditional on the prize contract: a dishonest or later nontransferable NFT can leave a winner without the promised prize even though the sponsor can receive 95% of sales. Reviewers disagree on whether this is a High design violation, a Medium integration flaw or an explicitly limited prize-trust guarantee. The disagreement arises from conflicting scope language and remains open.

The second is a Low destination-safety failure. A sponsor can choose the address of a future raffle as its fixed recipient. After that raffle exists, the first raffle can send an ordinary ERC721 prize into it, where the prize becomes unrecoverable. A local honest-token reproduction passed. The demonstrated loss belongs to the sponsor-selected recipient; it does not show theft from an arbitrary EOA or another raffle's accounted funds.

Completed testing provides substantial evidence for ordinary custody, allocation, authorization and lifecycle behavior. It does not remove the prize-trust issue, prove all external integrations, or make weakly exercised invariant handlers comprehensive. There is no demonstrated unconditional Critical exploit or production quote-ledger insolvency in the reconciled evidence.

The register contains 21 findings, observations, configuration risks, closed candidates and advisory entries—not 21 vulnerabilities. Its 190 attribution records plus the two late Pashov attributions preserve every adopted original ID, including rejected candidates and conflicting severity judgments. Eighteen sealed first-pass report paths underpin the combined reconciliation; repeated paths, report copies, functions and model agreement are not independent votes. OpenKritt's four native candidate records are separately identified and deduplicated. See the [original reconciliation](/Users/hishamel-husseini/Documents/projects/raffle-fun/audits/2026-10-21-r001/reconciliation/RECONCILIATION.md), [sealed addendum](/Users/hishamel-husseini/Documents/projects/raffle-fun/audits/2026-10-21-r001/reconciliation/RECONCILIATION-ADDENDUM.md), [updated register](/Users/hishamel-husseini/Documents/projects/raffle-fun/audits/2026-10-21-r001/reconciliation/findings-register-final-draft.json) and [late Pashov supplement](/Users/hishamel-husseini/Documents/projects/raffle-fun/audits/2026-10-21-r001/reconciliation/RECONCILIATION-PASHOV-SUPPLEMENT.md).

## Scope and method

Production scope comprises `Raffle.sol`, `RaffleFactory.sol`, `interfaces/IRaffle.sol`, `interfaces/IRaffleFactory.sol` and `libraries/RaffleConstants.sol`, plus 31 exact reachable dependency files and DESIGN.md. The clean review package excludes repository tests, historical audits and scanner outputs from the independent source-first passes. Later test-exposed, tool-assisted and cross-review work is declared separately; it does not overwrite the sealed first passes.

The architecture is immutable factory-created raffle clones with transferable bearer tickets. Entry purchases fund quote-token liabilities; authenticated VRF chooses an entry; settlement allocates 95/5 for an NFT outcome or 80/15/5 for a cash outcome; timeouts allow full ticket refunds. Fixed recipient claims can be released independently. Correct quote accounting assumes the configured canonical quote token transfers exact amounts without fees or rebasing. ERC165, receiver callbacks and ownerOf are statements made by the selected NFT contract, not independent proof of its honesty or permanent transferability.

The [authority, lifecycle, callback and rollback map](/Users/hishamel-husseini/Documents/projects/raffle-fun/audits/2026-10-21-r001/runs/SUP-A2/attempt-01/FIRST-PASS.md:21) details actors, every transition and independently derived properties.

## Findings

### RF-001 — Prize delivery is conditional while NFT-outcome proceeds are independently payable

**Severity:** High under the explicit untrusted-prize DESIGN requirement; Medium or Low/integration risk under other reviewers' interpretation of the honest, standards-compliant prize assumption. **Confidence:** high in the reachable behavior; unresolved classification because the scope statements conflict.

A sponsor chooses a prize contract that either fabricates escrow/delivery statements or genuinely escrows an NFT and later refuses, pauses or revokes transferability. The factory checks that token's callback, Active status and ownerOf response. Buyers then purchase entries and the normal VRF path resolves NftWon. Settlement makes sponsor proceeds and protocol fees available without first delivering the prize. A prior successful payout is not rolled back by a later failed redemption, and NftWon has no failed-delivery refund transition.

The sponsor needs control over the selected collection's dishonest implementation or relevant transfer authority, or an external collection failure must occur. Quote-token or VRF compromise is not required. The economic exposure is 95% of sales paid to the sponsor while the winner lacks an enforceable promised NFT. The quote ledger can remain exactly solvent throughout. This is not demonstrated against a truthful NFT that stays transferable, and no other clone is drained.

Source anchors: [factory admission and escrow](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/clean-context/packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol:127), [prize receipt](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/clean-context/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:416), [redemption and verification](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/clean-context/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:309), [independent proceeds release](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/clean-context/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:375) and [terminal allocation](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/clean-context/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:533). The scope conflict is recorded between DESIGN.md and IRaffle.sol:12–15. Earlier sealed fabrication mocks support a concrete artificial-token path; their separate ownership ledger illustrates dishonest semantics rather than proving the value or behavior of a deployed collection. Incoming claimed proofs are not automatically independent validation.

Daybreak Simao H-1 through H-5 cover different functions of this economic chain. Late Pashov findings 1 and 2 have confidence 90, not an assigned security severity. Claude TIA-1/TOB-S6-3 and Gemini FP-M-02 use Medium; Claude SUP-03 calls it a Low integration risk and explicitly not a code defect. Those judgments remain visible. No reviewer statement is treated as owner risk acceptance.

Before implementation, specify whether the product promises enforceable prize delivery or only interaction with approved/trusted collection semantics. An allowlist can restrict exposure but cannot itself prevent later upgrades, pauses or seizure. A funded failure fallback must retain all quote amounts it promises, including protocol fees, and handle settlement and payout order explicitly. Simply checking ownerOf again does not authenticate a malicious token. No patch was applied.

### RF-002 — A future clone recipient bypasses creation-time destination screening

**Severity:** Low. **Confidence:** high for the demonstrated sponsor-return path.

A sponsor configures raffle A's immutable recipient as the predictable address of future raffle B. That address has no code and is not yet registered, so creation checks accept it. B is then normally deployed. If A refunds or takes the cash branch, anyone can call releaseSponsorPrize; its plain transferFrom sends A's NFT to B without repeating the runtime protocol-destination screen used by quote payouts. B exposes exits only for its own configured prize, leaving A's prize stuck.

The root reproduction used an honest ERC721 and both real clones. It confirms cross-clone asset movement and sponsor-selected own loss. Quote payout screening can instead leave A's sponsor proceeds unclaimable. The proof does not show an attacker choosing an unrelated victim's recipient. It also does not show B redeeming an A ticket: redemption requires the current owner to originate the call, which B cannot do.

Source anchors: [CREATE clone and registration](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/clean-context/packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol:105), [recipient validation](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/clean-context/packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol:163), [sponsor prize release](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/clean-context/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:395) and [runtime quote screen](/Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/clean-context/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:564). Reproduction: [RecipientValidation.t.sol](/Users/hishamel-husseini/Documents/projects/raffle-fun/audits/2026-10-21-r001/reconciliation/recipient-validation/RecipientValidation.t.sol) and [passing log](/Users/hishamel-husseini/Documents/projects/raffle-fun/audits/2026-10-21-r001/runs/TOOL-RECIPIENT-VALIDATION/attempt-01/stdout.txt).

Simao J-4 rejects the candidate as self-harm; Gemini's grouped FP-M-01 assigns Medium; Claude SUP-01 assigns Low. The register retains the Low destination-invariant defect and its strict preconditions. Apply a consistent runtime NFT destination policy if this invariant is required. Refusing the transfer prevents cross-clone movement but does not recover an immutable stranded claim; any recovery mechanism requires a separate authority and design decision. Changing CREATE to CREATE2 or adding address randomness is not a complete recovery or destination-safety solution.

These entries remain distinct from the two root causes. Full original IDs, source lines, actor capabilities, proof status, exclusions, remedies and re-audit properties are in the linked register.

## Test assurance and remediation-proposal quality

The four-mutant campaign tested fee allocation, an owner guard, a deadline comparison and disabled purchases in disposable copies. All four compiled and were killed by existing unit/fuzz/security tests. All four initially survived short invariant runs. The fee mutant was eventually killed at the larger recorded run count, while completely disabled purchases still passed strict invariants because failures were caught inside the handler. This constrains the meaning of large successful call counters. See [mutation report](/Users/hishamel-husseini/Documents/projects/raffle-fun/audits/2026-10-21-r001/runs/TOOL-MUTATION-QUALITY/SUMMARY.md).

| AQ-001 | Swallowed reverts/no-op paths can leave every economic action inactive while invariants pass. |
| AQ-002 | Handlers select the actual ticket owner, so they do not exercise the adversarial caller needed to expose owner-check deletion. |
| AQ-003 | Deadline prefilters omit the forbidden exact boundary and can conceal rejection-boundary mutations. |
| AQ-004 | Independent allocation checks are useful, but short-run branch reachability is weak and some ghost values follow implementation state. |
| AQ-005 | The standalone Python model does not roll back lazy settlement on rejected unauthorized redemption. Solidity does roll back; passing Python tests are not an equivalence proof. |
| AQ-006 | Eleven of 52 historical mutation definitions do not match the current target. Invalid definitions are not surviving mutants and must not inflate the score. |
| AQ-007 | Partial or rejected workflows, missing source-context files and uncertain model identity must not be reported as completed assurance. Excluded tests do not establish repository-wide test absence. |
| AQ-008 | The late Pashov Option C patch is unvalidated and incorrectly migrates zero terminal balances when NftWon is still unsettled, leaving the pot outside its proposed refund liability. This is a flaw in a suggestion, not frozen production code. |

The proposed Option C is excluded from recommended implementation. Any delivery fallback must cover pre-settlement and settled NftWon, move each liability exactly once, retain all promised money and define successful delivery and previously paid claims. No proposal has been applied or accepted by the owner.
